# repose_ui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/repose-ui/^0.21.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#views-modifiers-and-layout)Views, Modifiers, and Layout

Repose UI is built around three core ideas:

- `View`: an immutable description of a UI node.
- `Modifier`: layout, styling, and interaction hints attached to a- `View`.
- Layout + paint: a separate pass (`layout_and_paint`) that turns the`View`tree into a`Scene`+ hit regions using the Taffy layout engine.

[§](https://docs.rs#views)Views

A `View` is a lightweight value that describes *what* to show, not *how* it is
rendered. It is cheap to create and you are expected to rebuild the entire
view tree on each frame:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use repose_core::*;
use repose_ui::*;
fn Counter(count: i32, on_inc: impl Fn() + 'static) -> View {
    Column(Modifier::new().padding(16.0)).child((
        Text(format!("Count = {count}")),
        Button("Increment".into_children(), on_inc),
    ))
}
```
Internally, a `View` has:

- `id: ViewId`- assigned during composition/layout.
- `kind: ViewKind`- which widget it is (Text, Button, ScrollV, etc.).
- `modifier: Modifier`- layout/styling/interaction metadata.
- `children: Vec<View>`- owned child views.

Views are *pure data*: they do not hold state or references into platform
APIs. State lives in signals / `remember_*` and platform integration happens
in the runner (`repose-platform`).

[§](https://docs.rs#modifiers)Modifiers

`Modifier` describes *how* a view participates in layout and hit‑testing:

- Size hints: `size`,`width`,`height`,`min_size`,`max_size`,`fill_max_size`,`fill_max_width`,`fill_max_height`.
- Box model: `padding`,`padding_values`.
- Visuals: `background`,`background_brush`,`border`,`clip_rounded`,`alpha`,`transform`.
- Flex / grid: `flex_grow`,`flex_shrink`,`flex_basis`,`align_self`,`justify_content`,`align_items`,`grid`,`grid_span`.
- Positioning: `absolute()`,`offset(..)`for overlay / Stack / FABs.
- Interaction: `clickable()`, pointer callbacks,`on_scroll`,`semantics`.
- Custom paint: `painter`(used by`repose-canvas`).

Example:

```
use repose_core::*;
use repose_ui::*;
fn CardExample() -> View {
    Box(
        Modifier::new()
            .padding(16.0)
            .background(theme().surface)
            .border(1.0, theme().outline, 8.0)
            .clip_rounded(8.0),
    )
    .child(Text("Hello, Repose!"))
}
```
Modifiers are merged into a Taffy `Style` inside `layout_and_paint`. Most
values are specified in density‑independent pixels (dp) and converted to
physical pixels (`px`) using the current `Density` local.

[§](https://docs.rs#layout-1)Layout

Layout is a pure function:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
pub fn layout_and_paint(
    root: &View,
    size_px: (u32, u32),
    textfield_states: &HashMap<u64, Rc<RefCell<TextFieldState>>>,
    interactions: &Interactions,
    focused: Option<u64>,
) -> (Scene, Vec<HitRegion>, Vec<SemNode>);
```
It:

- Clones the root `View`and assigns stable`ViewId`s.
- Builds a parallel Taffy tree and computes layout for the given window size.
- Walks the tree to:
- Emit `SceneNode`s for visuals (rects, text, images, scrollbars, etc.).
- Build `HitRegion`s for input routing (clicks, pointer events, scroll).
- Build `SemNode`s for accessibility / semantics.

- Emit

`Row`, `Column`, `Stack`, `Grid`, `ScrollV` and `ScrollXY` are all special
`ViewKind`s that map into Taffy styles and additional paint/hit logic.

Because layout + paint are separate from the platform runner, you can reuse the same UI code on desktop, Android, and other platforms.

[77](#77)    pub fn new_with_tabs(tabs: Vec<PanelId>) -> Self {

[79](#79)            root: DockNode {
[80](#80)                id: 1,

[90](#90)    pub fn from_root(root: DockNode, max_node_id: u64) -> Self {

[94](#94)            root,
[95](#95)            next_id: max_node_id + 1,

[98](#98)        st

[100](#100)
[101](#101)    fn alloc_id(&mut self) -> u64 {
[102](#102)        let id = self.next_id;
[103](#103)        self.next_id += 1;
[104](#104)        id

[109](#109)    }

[115](#115)
[116](#116)    pub fn remove_panel(&mut self, pid: PanelId) -> bool {

[118](#118)        if removed {
[119](#119)            normalize_node(&mut self.root);

[123](#123)
[124](#124)    pub fn set_active(&mut self, tabs_node_id: u64, pid: PanelId) {
[125](#125)        if let Some(n) = find_node_mut(&mut self.root, tabs_node_id)
[126](#126)            && let DockKind::Tabs { tabs, active } = &mut n.kind
[127](#127)            && tabs.contains(&pid)
[128](#128)        {
[129](#129)            *active = Some(pid);
[130](#130)        }
[131](#131)    }
[132](#132)
[133](#133)    pub fn set_split_ratio(&mut self, split_node_id: u64, ratio: f32) {
[134](#134)        let ratio = ratio.clamp(0.05, 0.95);
[135](#135)        if let Some(n) = find_node_mut(&mut self.root, split_node_id)
[136](#136)            && let DockKind::Split { ratio: r, .. } = &mut n.kind
[137](#137)        {
[138](#138)            *r = ratio;
[139](#139)        }
[140](#140)    }
[141](#141)
[142](#142)    pub fn dock_panel(&mut self, target_node_id: u64, zone: DropZone, pid: PanelId) -> bool {
[143](#143)        self.remove_panel_no_normalize(pid);
[144](#144)
[145](#145)        let result = match zone {
[146](#146)            DropZone::Center => self.insert_as_tab(target_node_id, pid),
[147](#147)            DropZone::Left | DropZone::Right | DropZone::Top | DropZone::Bottom => {
[148](#148)                self.insert_as_split(target_node_id, zone, pid)
[149](#149)            }
[150](#150)            DropZone::Float => false,
[151](#151)        };
[152](#152)
[153](#153)        self.normalize();
[154](#154)        result
[155](#155)    }
[156](#156)
[157](#157)    fn insert_as_tab(&mut self, target_node_id: u64, pid: PanelId) -> bool {
[158](#158)        let Some(n) = find_node_mut(&mut self.root, target_node_id) else {
[159](#159)            return false;
[160](#160)        };
[161](#161)
[162](#162)        match &mut n.kind {
[163](#163)            DockKind::Tabs { tabs, active } => {
[164](#164)                if !tabs.contains(&pid) {
[165](#165)                    tabs.push(pid);
[166](#166)                }
[167](#167)                *active = Some(pid);
[168](#168)                self.normalize();
[169](#169)                true
[170](#170)            }
[171](#171)            DockKind::Empty => {
[172](#172)                n.kind = DockKind::Tabs {
[173](#173)                    tabs: vec![pid],
[174](#174)                    active: Some(pid),
[175](#175)                };
[176](#176)                self.normalize();
[177](#177)                true
[178](#178)            }
[179](#179)            DockKind::Split { .. } => false,
[180](#180)        }
[181](#181)    }
[182](#182)
[183](#183)    fn insert_as_split(&mut self, target_node_id: u64, zone: DropZone, pid: PanelId) -> bool {
[184](#184)        let new_tabs_id = self.alloc_id();
[186](#186)        let new_split_id = self.alloc_id();
[187](#187)
[188](#188)        let Some(n) = find_node_mut(&mut self.root, target_node_id) else {
[189](#189)            return false;
[190](#190)        };
[191](#191)
[192](#192)        let old_kind = std::mem::replace(&mut n.kind, DockKind::Empty);
[193](#193)
[194](#194)        let dir = match zone {
[195](#195)            DropZone::Left | DropZone::Right => SplitDir::Horizontal,
[196](#196)            DropZone::Top | DropZone::Bottom => SplitDir::Vertical,
[197](#197)            _ => SplitDir::Horizontal,
[198](#198)        };
[199](#199)
[200](#200)        let new_tabs = DockNode {
[201](#201)            id: new_tabs_id,
[202](#202)            kind: DockKind::Tabs {
[203](#203)                tabs: vec![pid],
[204](#204)                active: Some(pid),
[205](#205)            },
[206](#206)        };
[207](#207)
[208](#208)        let old_node = DockNode {
[210](#210)            id: target_node_id,
[211](#211)            kind: old_kind,
[212](#212)        };
[213](#213)
[214](#214)        let (a, b) = match zone {
[215](#215)            DropZone::Left | DropZone::Top => (Box::new(new_tabs), Box::new(old_node)),
[216](#216)            DropZone::Right | DropZone::Bottom => (Box::new(old_node), Box::new(new_tabs)),
[217](#217)            _ => (Box::new(old_node), Box::new(new_tabs)),
[218](#218)        };
[219](#219)
[220](#220)        n.id = new_split_id;
[222](#222)        n.kind = DockKind::Split {
[223](#223)            dir,
[224](#224)            ratio: 0.5,
[225](#225)            a,
[226](#226)            b,
[227](#227)        };
[228](#228)
[229](#229)        self.normalize();
[230](#230)        true
[231](#231)    }

[251](#251)pub fn DockArea(

[266](#266)        RefCell::new(None::<SplitDrag>)
[267](#267)    });

[269](#269)    let float_target = {
[272](#272)        let state = state.clone();

[274](#274)        let cb_pop = callbacks.on_popout.clone();
[275](#275)
[276](#276)        Box(Modifier::new()
[277](#277)            .fill_max_size()
[278](#278)            .z_index(-1000.0)
[279](#279)            .on_drop(move |ev| {
[280](#280)                let Some(p) = ev.payload.as_ref().downcast_ref::<DockTabPayload>() else {
[282](#282)                    return false;

[285](#285)                    return false;

[291](#291)

[293](#293)                true
[294](#294)            }))
[295](#295)    };
[296](#296)
[297](#297)    let root_view = {
[299](#299)        let st = state.borrow().clone();
[300](#300)        render_node(
[301](#301)            &st.root,
[302](#302)            ®istry,
[303](#303)            &state,
[304](#304)            &callbacks,
[305](#305)            &hover_sig,
[306](#306)            &drag_active,
[307](#307)            &split_hover,
[308](#308)            &split_drag,
[309](#309)            key.as_str(),
[310](#310)        )
[311](#311)    };
[312](#312)

[314](#314)        Box(Modifier::new()

[333](#333)fn render_node(
[334](#334)    node: &DockNode,
[335](#335)    registry: &Rc<HashMap<PanelId, DockPanel>>,
[336](#336)    state: &Rc<RefCell<DockState>>,
[337](#337)    callbacks: &DockCallbacks,
[338](#338)    hover_sig: &Signal<Option<HoverHint>>,
[339](#339)    drag_active: &Signal<bool>,
[340](#340)    split_hover: &Signal<Option<u64>>,
[341](#341)    split_drag: &Rc<RefCell<Option<SplitDrag>>>,
[342](#342)    key_prefix: &str,
[343](#343)) -> View {
[344](#344)    match &node.kind {
[345](#345)        DockKind::Empty => Box(Modifier::new()
[346](#346)            .fill_max_size()
[347](#347)            .background(theme().surface)
[348](#348)            .key(node.id))
[349](#349)        .child(Box(Modifier::new().fill_max_size()).child(Text("Empty").color(theme().on_surface))),
[350](#350)
[351](#351)        DockKind::Tabs { tabs, active } => render_tabs(
[352](#352)            node.id,
[353](#353)            tabs,
[354](#354)            *active,
[355](#355)            registry,
[356](#356)            state,
[357](#357)            callbacks,
[358](#358)            hover_sig,
[359](#359)            drag_active,
[360](#360)            split_hover,
[361](#361)            key_prefix,
[362](#362)        ),
[363](#363)
[364](#364)        DockKind::Split { dir, ratio, a, b } => render_split(
[365](#365)            node.id,
[366](#366)            *dir,
[367](#367)            *ratio,
[368](#368)            a,
[369](#369)            b,
[370](#370)            registry,
[371](#371)            state,
[372](#372)            callbacks,
[373](#373)            hover_sig,
[374](#374)            drag_active,
[375](#375)            split_hover,
[376](#376)            split_drag,
[377](#377)            key_prefix,
[378](#378)        ),
[379](#379)    }

[381](#381)
[382](#382)fn render_tabs(
[383](#383)    node_id: u64,
[384](#384)    tabs: &Vec<PanelId>,
[385](#385)    active: Option<PanelId>,
[386](#386)    registry: &Rc<HashMap<PanelId, DockPanel>>,
[387](#387)    state: &Rc<RefCell<DockState>>,
[388](#388)    callbacks: &DockCallbacks,
[389](#389)    hover_sig: &Signal<Option<HoverHint>>,
[390](#390)    drag_active: &Signal<bool>,
[391](#391)    _split_hover: &Signal<Option<u64>>,
[392](#392)    key_prefix: &str,
[393](#393)) -> View {
[394](#394)    let th = theme();
[395](#395)
[396](#396)    let active_pid = active.or_else(|| tabs.first().copied());
[398](#398)
[399](#399)    let tabbar_rect = remember_with_key(format!("dock:tabbar_rect:{key_prefix}:{node_id}"), || {
[400](#400)        RefCell::new(Rect::default())
[401](#401)    });
[402](#402)
[403](#403)    let mut bar_mod = Modifier::new()
[404](#404)        .fill_max_width()
[405](#405)        .height(40.0)
[406](#406)        .background(th.surface)
[407](#407)        .border(1.0, th.outline, 0.0)
[408](#408)        .padding(6.0)
[409](#409)        .painter({
[410](#410)            let tabbar_rect = tabbar_rect.clone();
[411](#411)            move |_scene, r, _alpha| *tabbar_rect.borrow_mut() = r
[412](#412)        });
[413](#413)
[414](#414)    if drag_active.get() {
[415](#415)        bar_mod = bar_mod.on_drop({
[416](#416)            let state = state.clone();
[417](#417)            let tabbar_rect = tabbar_rect.clone();
[418](#418)            let hover_sig = hover_sig.clone();
[419](#419)            let drag_active = drag_active.clone();
[420](#420)
[421](#421)            move |ev| {
[422](#422)                let Some(p) = ev.payload.as_ref().downcast_ref::<DockTabPayload>() else {
[423](#423)                    return false;
[424](#424)                };
[425](#425)
[426](#426)                let mut st = state.borrow_mut();
[427](#427)
[428](#428)                st.remove_panel_no_normalize(p.panel_id);
[430](#430)
[431](#431)                let r = *tabbar_rect.borrow();
[432](#432)                let t = if r.w > 1.0 {
[433](#433)                    ((ev.position.x - r.x) / r.w).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
[434](#434)                } else {
[435](#435)                    1.0
[436](#436)                };
[437](#437)
[438](#438)                if let Some(n) = find_node_mut(&mut st.root, node_id) {
[439](#439)                    if matches!(n.kind, DockKind::Empty) {
[440](#440)                        n.kind = DockKind::Tabs {
[441](#441)                            tabs: Vec::new(),
[442](#442)                            active: None,
[443](#443)                        };
[444](#444)                    }
[445](#445)
[446](#446)                    if let DockKind::Tabs { tabs, active } = &mut n.kind {
[447](#447)                        tabs.retain(|&x| x != p.panel_id);
[448](#448)                        let idx =
[449](#449)                            ((t * (tabs.len() as f32 + 1.0)).floor() as usize).min(tabs.len());
[450](#450)                        tabs.insert(idx, p.panel_id);
[451](#451)                        *active = Some(p.panel_id);
[452](#452)                    }
[453](#453)                }
[454](#454)
[455](#455)                st.normalize();
[456](#456)
[457](#457)                hover_sig.set(None);
[458](#458)                drag_active.set(false);
[459](#459)                request_frame();
[460](#460)                true
[461](#461)            }
[462](#462)        });
[463](#463)    }
[464](#464)
[465](#465)    let tab_bar = Row(bar_mod).with_children(
[466](#466)        tabs.iter()
[467](#467)            .copied()
[468](#468)            .filter_map(|pid| {
[469](#469)                let panel = registry.get(&pid)?;
[470](#470)                let is_active = Some(pid) == active_pid;
[471](#471)
[472](#472)                let state_set = state.clone();
[473](#473)                let title = panel.title.clone();
[474](#474)
[475](#475)                let drag_pid = pid;
[476](#476)
[477](#477)                let cb_close = callbacks.on_close.clone();
[478](#478)                let cb_pop = callbacks.on_popout.clone();
[479](#479)
[480](#480)                Some(
[481](#481)                    Stack(
[482](#482)                        Modifier::new()
[483](#483)                            .key(pid)
[484](#484)                            .height(32.0)
[485](#485)                            .padding(4.0)
[486](#486)                            .clip_rounded(th.shapes.small)
[487](#487)                            .background(if is_active {
[488](#488)                                th.primary.with_alpha(80)
[489](#489)                            } else {
[490](#490)                                th.surface
[491](#491)                            })
[492](#492)                            .border(1.0, th.outline, th.shapes.small),
[493](#493)                    )
[494](#494)                    .child((
[495](#495)                        Box(Modifier::new()
[496](#496)                            .height(24.0)
[497](#497)                            .offset(None, Some(4.0), None, None)
[498](#498)                            .clickable()
[499](#499)                            .cursor(CursorIcon::Grab)
[500](#500)                            .on_pointer_down({
[501](#501)                                let state_set = state_set.clone();
[502](#502)                                move |_| {
[503](#503)                                    state_set.borrow_mut().set_active(node_id, pid);
[504](#504)                                    request_frame();
[505](#505)                                }
[506](#506)                            })
[507](#507)                            .on_drag_start({
[508](#508)                                let drag_active = drag_active.clone();
[509](#509)                                move |_start| {
[510](#510)                                    drag_active.set(true);
[511](#511)                                    Some(Rc::new(DockTabPayload { panel_id: drag_pid })
[512](#512)                                        as Rc<dyn Any>)
[513](#513)                                }
[514](#514)                            })
[515](#515)                            .on_drag_end({
[516](#516)                                let hover_sig = hover_sig.clone();
[517](#517)                                let drag_active = drag_active.clone();
[518](#518)                                move |_end| {
[519](#519)                                    drag_active.set(false);
[520](#520)                                    hover_sig.set(None);
[521](#521)                                }
[522](#522)                            }))
[523](#523)                        .child(
[524](#524)                            Row(Modifier::new().height(24.0))
[525](#525)                                .child((Text(title).color(th.on_surface),)),
[526](#526)                        ),
[527](#527)                        Row(Modifier::new().absolute().height(24.0).offset(
[528](#528)                            None,
[529](#529)                            Some(4.0),
[530](#530)                            Some(2.0),
[531](#531)                            None,
[532](#532)                        ))
[533](#533)                        .child((
[534](#534)                            if let Some(pop) = cb_pop {
[535](#535)                                Box(Modifier::new()
[536](#536)                                    .clickable()
[537](#537)                                    .on_pointer_down(move |_| pop(pid))
[538](#538)                                    .padding(2.0))
[539](#539)                                .child(Text("↗").size(12.0))
[540](#540)                            } else {
[541](#541)                                Box(Modifier::new())
[542](#542)                            },
[543](#543)                            if let Some(close) = cb_close {
[544](#544)                                Box(Modifier::new()
[545](#545)                                    .clickable()
[546](#546)                                    .on_pointer_down(move |_| close(pid))
[547](#547)                                    .padding(2.0))
[548](#548)                                .child(Text("×").size(12.0))
[549](#549)                            } else {
[550](#550)                                Box(Modifier::new())
[551](#551)                            },
[552](#552)                        )),
[553](#553)                    )),
[554](#554)                )
[555](#555)            })
[556](#556)            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
[557](#557)    );
[558](#558)
[559](#559)    let content = if let Some(pid) = active_pid {
[561](#561)        if let Some(panel) = registry.get(&pid) {
[562](#562)            (panel.content)()
[563](#563)        } else {
[564](#564)            Text("Missing panel").color(th.error)
[565](#565)        }
[566](#566)    } else {
[567](#567)        Text("No tabs").color(th.on_surface)
[568](#568)    };
[569](#569)
[570](#570)    let overlay = dock_drop_overlay(node_id, state, hover_sig, drag_active, key_prefix);
[572](#572)
[573](#573)    let tab_h = 40.0;
[574](#574)
[575](#575)    Stack(Modifier::new().fill_max_size().key(node_id)).child((
[576](#576)        Column(Modifier::new().fill_max_size()).child((
[577](#577)            tab_bar,
[578](#578)            Box(Modifier::new().fill_max_size().background(th.background))
[579](#579)                .child(Box(Modifier::new().fill_max_size().padding(8.0)).child(content)),
[580](#580)        )),
[581](#581)        Box(Modifier::new()
[582](#582)            .absolute()
[583](#583)            .offset(Some(0.0), Some(tab_h), Some(0.0), Some(0.0)))
[584](#584)        .child(overlay),
[585](#585)    ))

[587](#587)
[588](#588)fn dock_drop_overlay(
[589](#589)    node_id: u64,
[590](#590)    state: &Rc<RefCell<DockState>>,
[591](#591)    hover_sig: &Signal<Option<HoverHint>>,
[592](#592)    drag_active: &Signal<bool>,
[593](#593)    key_prefix: &str,
[594](#594)) -> View {
[595](#595)    let th = theme();
[596](#596)    if !drag_active.get() {
[597](#597)        return Box(Modifier::new());
[598](#598)    }
[599](#599)
[600](#600)    let zone_dp = 48.0;
[601](#601)
[602](#602)    let hover = hover_sig.get();
[603](#603)
[604](#604)    let mk_zone = |zone: DropZone, m: Modifier| -> View {
[605](#605)        let state2 = state.clone();
[606](#606)        let hover2 = hover_sig.clone();
[607](#607)
[608](#608)        let label = match zone {
[609](#609)            DropZone::Center => " ",
[611](#611)            DropZone::Left => " ",
[612](#612)            DropZone::Right => " ",
[613](#613)            DropZone::Top => " ",
[614](#614)            DropZone::Bottom => " ",
[615](#615)            DropZone::Float => " ",
[616](#616)        };
[617](#617)
[618](#618)        let highlight = if hover.as_ref() == Some(&HoverHint { node_id, zone }) {
[619](#619)            Stack(
[620](#620)                Modifier::new()
[621](#621)                    .fill_max_size()
[622](#622)                    .background(th.primary.with_alpha(51))
[623](#623)                    .border(2.0, th.primary, 0.0),
[624](#624)            )

[910](#910)fn remove_panel_in_node(node: &mut DockNode, pid: PanelId) -> bool {
[911](#911)    match &mut node.kind {
[912](#912)        DockKind::Empty => false,
[913](#913)
[914](#914)        DockKind::Tabs { tabs, active } => {
[915](#915)            let before = tabs.len();
[916](#916)            tabs.retain(|&x| x != pid);
[917](#917)            if tabs.len() != before {
[918](#918)                if active == &Some(pid) {
[919](#919)                    *active = tabs.first().copied();
[920](#920)                }
[921](#921)                if tabs.is_empty() {
[922](#922)                    node.kind = DockKind::Empty;
[923](#923)                }
[924](#924)                true
[925](#925)            } else {
[926](#926)                false
[927](#927)            }
[928](#928)        }
[929](#929)
[930](#930)        DockKind::Split { a, b, .. } => {
[931](#931)            let ra = remove_panel_in_node(a, pid);
[932](#932)            let rb = remove_panel_in_node(b, pid);
[933](#933)            ra || rb
[934](#934)        }
[935](#935)    }

[937](#937)
[938](#938)fn normalize_node(node: &mut DockNode) {
[939](#939)    match &mut node.kind {
[940](#940)        DockKind::Empty => {}
[941](#941)        DockKind::Tabs { tabs, active } => {
[942](#942)            if tabs.is_empty() {
[943](#943)                node.kind = DockKind::Empty;
[944](#944)            } else if active.is_none() || !tabs.contains(&active.unwrap()) {
[945](#945)                *active = tabs.first().copied();
[946](#946)            }
[947](#947)        }
[948](#948)        DockKind::Split { a, b, ratio, .. } => {
[949](#949)            *ratio = ratio.clamp(0.05, 0.95);
[950](#950)            normalize_node(a);
[951](#951)            normalize_node(b);
[952](#952)
[953](#953)            let a_empty = matches!(a.kind, DockKind::Empty);
[954](#954)            let b_empty = matches!(b.kind, DockKind::Empty);
[955](#955)
[956](#956)            if a_empty && !b_empty {
[958](#958)                node.kind = std::mem::replace(&mut b.kind, DockKind::Empty);
[959](#959)            } else if b_empty && !a_empty {
[960](#960)                node.kind = std::mem::replace(&mut a.kind, DockKind::Empty);
[961](#961)            } else if a_empty && b_empty {
[962](#962)                node.kind = DockKind::Empty;
[963](#963)            }
[964](#964)        }
[965](#965)    }
[966](#966)}

[92](#92)
[93](#93)pub fn Canvas(modifier: Modifier, on_draw: impl Fn(&mut DrawScope) + 'static) -> View {
[94](#94)    let painter = move |scene: &mut Scene, rect: Rect, _alpha: f32| {
[96](#96)        let mut scope = DrawScope {
[97](#97)            commands: Vec::new(),
[98](#98)            size: Size {
[99](#99)                width: rect.w.max(0.0),
[100](#100)                height: rect.h.max(0.0),
[101](#101)            },
[102](#102)        };
[103](#103)        on_draw(&mut scope);
[104](#104)
[105](#105)        let to_global = |r: Rect| Rect {
[107](#107)            x: rect.x + r.x,
[108](#108)            y: rect.y + r.y,
[109](#109)            w: r.w,
[110](#110)            h: r.h,
[111](#111)        };
[112](#112)
[113](#113)        for cmd in &scope.commands {
[114](#114)            match cmd {
[115](#115)                DrawCommand::Rect {
[116](#116)                    rect: r,
[117](#117)                    color,
[118](#118)                    radius,
[119](#119)                    stroke,
[120](#120)                } => {
[121](#121)                    scene.nodes.push(SceneNode::Rect {
[122](#122)                        rect: to_global(*r),
[123](#123)                        brush: Brush::Solid(*color),
[124](#124)                        radius: [*radius; 4],
[125](#125)                    });
[126](#126)                    if let Some((w, c)) = stroke {
[127](#127)                        scene.nodes.push(SceneNode::Border {
[128](#128)                            rect: to_global(*r),
[129](#129)                            color: *c,
[130](#130)                            width: *w,
[131](#131)                            radius: [*radius; 4],
[132](#132)                        });
[133](#133)                    }
[134](#134)                }
[135](#135)                DrawCommand::Ellipse {
[136](#136)                    center,
[137](#137)                    rx,
[138](#138)                    ry,
[139](#139)                    color,
[140](#140)                    stroke,
[141](#141)                } => {
[142](#142)                    let r = Rect {
[143](#143)                        x: center.x - *rx,
[144](#144)                        y: center.y - *ry,
[145](#145)                        w: 2.0 * *rx,
[146](#146)                        h: 2.0 * *ry,
[147](#147)                    };
[148](#148)                    scene.nodes.push(SceneNode::Ellipse {
[149](#149)                        rect: to_global(r),
[150](#150)                        brush: Brush::Solid(*color),
[151](#151)                    });
[152](#152)                    if let Some((w, c)) = stroke {
[153](#153)                        scene.nodes.push(SceneNode::EllipseBorder {
[154](#154)                            rect: to_global(r),
[155](#155)                            color: *c,
[156](#156)                            width: *w,
[157](#157)                        });
[158](#158)                    }
[159](#159)                }
[160](#160)                DrawCommand::Text {
[161](#161)                    text,
[162](#162)                    pos,
[163](#163)                    color,
[164](#164)                    size,
[165](#165)                } => {
[166](#166)                    scene.nodes.push(SceneNode::Text {
[167](#167)                        rect: Rect {
[168](#168)                            x: rect.x + pos.x,
[169](#169)                            y: rect.y + pos.y,
[170](#170)                            w: 0.0,
[171](#171)                            h: *size,
[172](#172)                        },
[173](#173)                        text: Arc::<str>::from(text.clone()),
[174](#174)                        color: *color,
[175](#175)                        size: *size,
[176](#176)                        font_family: None,
[177](#177)                        text_align: TextAlign::Unspecified,
[178](#178)                        font_weight: FontWeight::NORMAL,
[179](#179)                        font_style: FontStyle::Normal,
[180](#180)                        text_decoration: TextDecoration::default(),
[181](#181)                        letter_spacing: 0.0,
[182](#182)                        line_height: 0.0,
[183](#183)                    });
[184](#184)                }
[185](#185)            }
[186](#186)        }
[187](#187)    };
[188](#188)
[189](#189)    let mut m = modifier.painter(painter);
[191](#191)    let has_size = m.size.is_some()
[192](#192)        || m.width.is_some()
[193](#193)        || m.height.is_some()
[194](#194)        || m.fill_max.is_some()
[195](#195)        || m.fill_max_w.is_some()
[196](#196)        || m.fill_max_h.is_some();
[197](#197)    if !has_size {
[198](#198)        m = m.size(100.0, 100.0);
[199](#199)    }
[200](#200)
[201](#201)    Box(m)
[202](#202)}

# ab_glyph - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ab_glyph/^0.2.32/

## Expand description

API for loading, scaling, positioning and rasterizing OpenType font glyphs.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ab_glyph::{point, Font, FontRef, Glyph};
let font = FontRef::try_from_slice(include_bytes!("../../dev/fonts/Exo2-Light.otf"))?;
// Get a glyph for 'q' with a scale & position.
let q_glyph: Glyph = font
    .glyph_id('q')
    .with_scale_and_position(24.0, point(100.0, 0.0));
// Draw it.
if let Some(q) = font.outline_glyph(q_glyph) {
    q.draw(|x, y, c| { /* draw pixel `(x, y)` with coverage: `c` */ });
}
```

# anyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/anyhow/^1/

## Expand description

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error
type for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use anyhow::Result; fn get_cluster_info() -> Result<ClusterMap> { let config = std::fs::read_to_string("cluster.json")?; let map: ClusterMap = serde_json::from_str(&config)?; Ok(map) }`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like “No such file or directory” can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use anyhow::{Context, Result}; fn main() -> Result<()> { ... it.detach().context("Failed to detach the important thing")?; let content = std::fs::read(path) .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read instrs from {}", path))?; ... }``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.downcast_ref::<DataStoreError>() { Some(DataStoreError::Censored(_)) => Ok(Poll::Ready(REDACTED_CONTENT)), None => Err(error), }`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use thiserror::Error; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum FormatError { #[error("Invalid header (expected {expected:?}, got {found:?})")] InvalidHeader { expected: String, found: String, }, #[error("Missing attribute: {0}")] MissingAttribute(String), }`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err(anyhow!("Missing attribute: {}", missing));`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!("Missing attribute: {}", missing);`

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled “std” feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[dependencies]
anyhow = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow’s error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)as format_err;

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

# bytemuck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bytemuck/^1.25.0/

## Expand description

This crate gives small utilities for casting between plain data types.

[§](https://docs.rs#basics)Basics

Data comes in five basic forms in Rust, so we have five basic casting functions:

- `T`uses- `cast`
- `&T`uses- `cast_ref`
- `&mut T`uses- `cast_mut`
- `&[T]`uses- `cast_slice`
- `&mut [T]`uses- `cast_slice_mut`

Depending on the function, the [ NoUninit](https://docs.rs/trait.NoUninit.html) and/or

[traits are used to maintain memory safety.](https://docs.rs/trait.AnyBitPattern.html)

`AnyBitPattern`**Historical Note:** When the crate first started the [ Pod](https://docs.rs/trait.Pod.html) trait was used
instead, and so you may hear people refer to that, but it has the strongest
requirements and people eventually wanted the more fine-grained system, so
here we are. All types that impl

`Pod` have a blanket impl to also support
`NoUninit` and `AnyBitPattern`. The traits unfortunately do not have a
perfectly clean hierarchy for semver reasons.[§](https://docs.rs#failures)Failures

Some casts will never fail, and other casts might fail.

- `cast::<u32, f32>`always works (and- `f32::from_bits`
- `cast_ref::<[u8; 4], u32>`might fail if the specific array reference given at runtime doesn’t have alignment 4.

In addition to the “normal” forms of each function, which will panic on
invalid input, there’s also `try_` versions which will return a `Result`.

If you would like to statically ensure that a cast will work at runtime you
can use the `must_cast` crate feature and the `must_` casting functions. A
“must cast” that can’t be statically known to be valid will cause a
compilation error (and sometimes a very hard to read compilation error).

[§](https://docs.rs#using-your-own-types)Using Your Own Types

All the functions listed above are guarded by the [ Pod](https://docs.rs/trait.Pod.html) trait, which is a
sub-trait of the

[trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.Zeroable.html)

`Zeroable`If you enable the crate’s `derive` feature then these traits can be derived
on your own types. The derive macros will perform the necessary checks on
your type declaration, and trigger an error if your type does not qualify.

The derive macros might not cover all edge cases, and sometimes they will
error when actually everything is fine. As a last resort you can impl these
traits manually. However, these traits are `unsafe`, and you should
carefully read the requirements before using a manual implementation.

[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-features)Cargo Features

The crate supports Rust 1.34 when no features are enabled, and so there’s cargo features for thing that you might consider “obvious”.

The cargo features **do not** promise any particular MSRV, and they may
increase their MSRV in new versions.

- `derive`: Provide derive macros for the various traits.
- `extern_crate_alloc`: Provide utilities for- `alloc`related types such as Box and Vec.
- `zeroable_maybe_uninit`and- `zeroable_atomics`: Provide more- `Zeroable`
- `pod_saturating`: Provide more- `Pod`- `Zeroable`
- `wasm_simd`and- `aarch64_simd`: Support more SIMD types.
- `min_const_generics`: Provides appropriate impls for arrays of all lengths instead of just for a select list of array lengths.
- `must_cast`: Provides the- `must_`functions, which will compile error if the requested cast can’t be statically verified.
- `const_zeroed`: Provides a const version of the- `zeroed`function.

[§](https://docs.rs#related-crates)Related Crates

- `pack1`- `bytemuck`-compatible packed little-endian, big-endian and native-endian integer and floating point number types.

# cosmic_text - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cosmic-text/^0.19/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#cosmic-text)COSMIC Text

This library provides advanced text handling in a generic way. It provides abstractions for shaping, font discovery, font fallback, layout, rasterization, and editing. Shaping utilizes harfrust, font discovery utilizes fontdb, and the rasterization is optional and utilizes swash. The other features are developed internal to this library.

It is recommended that you start by creating a [ FontSystem](https://docs.rs/struct.FontSystem.html), after which you can create a

[, provide it with some text, and then inspect the layout it produces. At this point, you can use the](https://docs.rs/struct.Buffer.html)

`Buffer``SwashCache` to rasterize glyphs into either images or pixels.```
use cosmic_text::{Attrs, Color, FontSystem, SwashCache, Buffer, Metrics, Shaping};
// A FontSystem provides access to detected system fonts, create one per application
let mut font_system = FontSystem::new();
// A SwashCache stores rasterized glyphs, create one per application
let mut swash_cache = SwashCache::new();
// Text metrics indicate the font size and line height of a buffer
let metrics = Metrics::new(14.0, 20.0);
// A Buffer provides shaping and layout for a UTF-8 string, create one per text widget
let mut buffer = Buffer::new(&mut font_system, metrics);
// Borrow buffer together with the font system for more convenient method calls
let mut buffer = buffer.borrow_with(&mut font_system);
// Attributes indicate what font to choose
let attrs = Attrs::new();
// Set size and text
buffer.set_size(Some(80.0), Some(25.0));
buffer.set_text("Hello, Rust! 🦀\n", &attrs, Shaping::Advanced, None);
// Inspect the output runs
for run in buffer.layout_runs() {
    for glyph in run.glyphs.iter() {
        println!("{:#?}", glyph);
    }
}
// Create a default text color
let text_color = Color::rgb(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF);
// Draw the buffer (for performance, instead use SwashCache directly)
buffer.draw(&mut swash_cache, text_color, |x, y, w, h, color| {
    // Fill in your code here for drawing rectangles
});
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Angle](https://docs.rs/struct.Angle.html)
- Represents an angle in degrees or radians.
- [Attrs](https://docs.rs/struct.Attrs.html)
- Text attributes
- [Attrs](https://docs.rs/struct.AttrsList.html)- List
- List of text attributes to apply to a line
- [Attrs](https://docs.rs/struct.AttrsOwned.html)- Owned
- An owned version of `Attrs`
- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiParagraphs.html)- Paragraphs
- An iterator over the paragraphs in the input text.

# fontdb - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fontdb/^0.23.0/

## Expand description

`fontdb` is a simple, in-memory font database with CSS-like queries.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- The database can load fonts from files, directories and raw data (`Vec<u8>`).
- The database can match a font using CSS-like queries. See `Database::query`.
- The database can try to load system fonts. Currently, this is implemented by scanning predefined directories. The library does not interact with the system API.
- Provides a unique ID for each font face.

[§](https://docs.rs#non-goals)Non-goals

-
Advanced font properties querying.
 The database provides only storage and matching capabilities. For font properties querying you can use[ttf-parser](https://github.com/RazrFalcon/ttf-parser).
-
A font fallback mechanism.
 This library can be used to implement a font fallback mechanism, but it doesn’t implement one.
-
Application’s global database.
 The database doesn’t use`static`, therefore it’s up to the caller where it should be stored.
-
Font types support other than TrueType.

[§](https://docs.rs#font-vs-face)Font vs Face

A font is a collection of font faces. Therefore, a font face is a subset of a font. A simple font (*.ttf/*.otf) usually contains a single font face, but a font collection (*.ttc) can contain multiple font faces.

`fontdb` stores and matches font faces, not fonts.
Therefore, after loading a font collection with 5 faces (for example), the database will be populated
with 5 `FaceInfo` objects, all of which will be pointing to the same file or binary data.

[§](https://docs.rs#performance)Performance

The database performance is largely limited by the storage itself.
We are using [ttf-parser](https://github.com/RazrFalcon/ttf-parser), so the parsing should not be a bottleneck.

On my machine with Samsung SSD 860 and Gentoo Linux, it takes ~20ms to load 1906 font faces (most of them are from Google Noto collection) with a hot disk cache and ~860ms with a cold one.

On Mac Mini M1 it takes just 9ms to load 898 fonts.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

The library relies on memory-mapped files, which is inherently unsafe. But since we do not keep the files open it should be perfectly safe.

If you would like to use a persistent memory mapping of the font files,
then you can use the unsafe [ Database::make_shared_face_data](https://docs.rs/struct.Database.html#method.make_shared_face_data) function.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Database](https://docs.rs/struct.Database.html)
- A font database.
- [Face](https://docs.rs/struct.FaceInfo.html)- Info
- A single font face info.
- [ID](https://docs.rs/struct.ID.html)
- A unique per database face ID.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/struct.Query.html)
- A database query.
- [Weight](https://docs.rs/struct.Weight.html)
- Specifies the weight of glyphs in the font, their degree of blackness or stroke thickness.

# image - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/image/^0.25/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

This crate provides native rust implementations of image encoding and decoding as well as some
basic image manipulation functions. Additional documentation can currently also be found in the
[README.md file which is most easily viewed on
github](https://github.com/image-rs/image/blob/main/README.md).

There are two core problems for which this library provides solutions: a unified interface for image encodings and simple generic buffers for their content. It’s possible to use either feature without the other. The focus is on a small and stable set of common operations that can be supplemented by other specialized crates. The library also prefers safe solutions with few dependencies.

[§](https://docs.rs#high-level-api)High level API

Load images using [ ImageReader](https://docs.rs/struct.ImageReader.html):

```
use std::io::Cursor;
use image::ImageReader;
let img = ImageReader::open("myimage.png")?.decode()?;
let img2 = ImageReader::new(Cursor::new(bytes)).with_guessed_format()?.decode()?;
```
And save them using [ save](https://docs.rs/enum.DynamicImage.html#method.save) or

[methods:](https://docs.rs/enum.DynamicImage.html#method.write_to)

`write_to````
img.save("empty.jpg")?;
let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
img2.write_to(&mut Cursor::new(&mut bytes), image::ImageFormat::Png)?;
```
With default features, the crate includes support for [many common image formats](https://docs.rs/codecs/index.html#supported-formats).

[§](https://docs.rs#image-buffers)Image buffers

The two main types for storing images:

- `ImageBuffer`
- `DynamicImage`- `ImageBuffer`formats and supports conversions between them.

As well as a few more specialized options:

- `GenericImage`
- `GenericImageView`- `GenericImage`.
- `flat`

[§](https://docs.rs#low-level-encodingdecoding-api)Low level encoding/decoding API

Implementations of [ ImageEncoder](https://docs.rs/trait.ImageEncoder.html) provides low level control over encoding:

```
let encoder = JpegEncoder::new_with_quality(&mut writer, 95);
img.write_with_encoder(encoder)?;
```
While [ ImageDecoder](https://docs.rs/trait.ImageDecoder.html) and

[give access to more advanced decoding options:](https://docs.rs/trait.ImageDecoderRect.html)

`ImageDecoderRect````
let decoder = PngDecoder::new(&mut reader)?;
let icc = decoder.icc_profile();
let img = DynamicImage::from_decoder(decoder)?;
```

# lyon_path - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lyon_path/^1.0/

## Expand description

Data structures and traits to work with paths (vector graphics).

To build and consume paths, see the [builder](https://docs.rs/builder/index.html) and
[iterator](https://docs.rs/iterator/index.html) modules.

This crate is reexported in [lyon](https://docs.rs/lyon/).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use lyon_path::Path;
use lyon_path::math::{point};
use lyon_path::builder::*;
// Create a builder object to build the path.
let mut builder = Path::builder();
// Build a simple path.
let mut builder = Path::builder();
builder.begin(point(0.0, 0.0));
builder.line_to(point(1.0, 2.0));
builder.line_to(point(2.0, 0.0));
builder.line_to(point(1.0, 1.0));
builder.close();
// Generate the actual path object.
let path = builder.build();
for event in &path {
    println!("{:?}", event);
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# lyon_tessellation - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lyon_tessellation/^1.0/

## Expand description

Tessellation of 2D fill and stroke operations.

This crate is reexported in [lyon](https://docs.rs/lyon/).

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The most interesting types and traits of this crate are:

- [FillTessellator](https://docs.rs/struct.FillTessellator.html)- Tessellator for complex path fill operations.
- [StrokeTessellator](https://docs.rs/struct.StrokeTessellator.html)- Tessellator for complex path stroke operations.
- `GeometryBuilder`- [geometry_builder module](https://docs.rs/geometry_builder/index.html)) which the above two are built on. This trait provides an interface for types that help with building and assembling the vertices and triangles that form the tessellation, usually in the form of arbitrary vertex and index buffers.

[§](https://docs.rs#the-tessellation-pipeline)The tessellation pipeline

The figure above shows a simplified summary of each step of the fill tessellation pipeline.

[§](https://docs.rs#the-input-iterators)The input: iterators

The path tessellators are not tied to a particular data structure. Instead they consume
iterators of flattened path events.
A [Path struct](https://docs.rs/lyon_path/*/lyon_path/struct.Path.html) in the crate
[lyon_path](https://docs.rs/lyon_path/*/lyon_path/) is provided for convenience
(but is optional).

[§](https://docs.rs#the-output-geometry-builders)The output: geometry builders

The tessellators are parametrized over a type implementing the
[GeometryBuilder trait](https://docs.rs/geometry_builder/trait.GeometryBuilder.html).
This trait provides some simple methods to add vertices and triangles, without enforcing
any particular representation for the resulting geometry. This is important because each
application will usually want to work with its own vertex type tailored a certain rendering
model.

Applications can implement the `GeometryBuilder<Point>` trait in order to
generate vertex buffers and index buffers with custom vertex types.

The structs [VertexBuffers](https://docs.rs/geometry_builder/struct.VertexBuffers.html) and
[geometry_builder::BuffersBuilder](https://docs.rs/geometry_builder/struct.BuffersBuilder.html) are provided
for convenience. `VertexBuffers<T>` is contains a `Vec<T>` for the vertices and a `Vec<u16>`
for the indices.

`BuffersBuilder` is generic over a `VertexConstructor<InputVertex, OutputVertex>` trait which
creates the application’s output vertices from the tessellator input vertices (either `FillVertex`
or `StrokeVertex`).

[§](https://docs.rs#rendering-the-tessellated-geometry)Rendering the tessellated geometry

The tessellators produce geometry in the form of vertex and index buffers which are expected
to be rendered using the equivalent of OpenGL’s `glDrawElements` with mode `GL_TRIANGLES` available
under various names in the different graphics APIs.
There is an [example](https://github.com/nical/lyon/tree/main/examples/wgpu) showing how
it can be done with wgpu.

[§](https://docs.rs#flattening-and-tolerance)Flattening and tolerance

Most tessellators in this crate currently operate on flattened paths (paths or shapes represented
by sequences of line segments). when paths contain bézier curves or arcs, the latter need to be
approximated with sequences of line segments. This approximation depends on a `tolerance` parameter
which represents the maximum distance between a curve and its flattened approximation.

More explanation about flattening and tolerance in the [lyon_geom crate](https://docs.rs/lyon_geom/#flattening).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

# pollster - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pollster/^0.4.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#pollster)Pollster

Pollster is an incredibly minimal async executor for Rust that lets you block a thread until a future completes.

```
use pollster::FutureExt as _;
let my_fut = async {};
let result = my_fut.block_on();
```
That’s it. That’s all it does. Nothing more, nothing less. No need to pull in 50 crates to evaluate a future.

[§](https://docs.rs#why-is-this-useful)Why is this useful?

Now that `async` functions are stable, we’re increasingly seeing libraries all over the Rust ecosystem expose `async`
APIs. This is great for those wanting to build highly concurrent web applications!

However, many of us are *not* building highly concurrent web applications, but end up faced with an `async` function
that we can’t easily call from synchronous code. If you’re in this position, then `pollster` is for you: it allows you
to evaluate a future in-place without spinning up a heavyweight runtime like `tokio` or `async_std`.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimalism)Minimalism

Pollster is built with the [UNIX ethos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_philosophy#Do_One_Thing_and_Do_It_Well) in
mind: do one thing, and do it well. It has no dependencies, compiles quickly, and is composed of only ~100 lines of
well-audited code.

[§](https://docs.rs#behaviour)Behaviour

Pollster will synchronously block the thread until a future completes. It will not spin: instead, it will place the thread into a waiting state until the future has been polled to completion.

[§](https://docs.rs#compatibility)Compatibility

Unfortunately, `pollster` will not work for *all* futures because some require a specific runtime or reactor. See
[here](https://rust-lang.github.io/async-book/08_ecosystem/00_chapter.html#determining-ecosystem-compatibility) for more
information about when and where `pollster` may be used. However, if you’re already pulling in the required dependencies
to create such a future in the first place, it’s likely that you already have a version of `block_on` in your dependency
tree that’s designed to poll your future, so use that instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#macro)Macro

When using the `macro` crate feature, an attribute-macro can be used to mark `async fn main()`:

Additionally if you have re-exported the crate with a different name then `pollster`, you have to specify it:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[pollster::main(crate = renamed_pollster)]
async fn main() {
    let my_fut = async {};
    my_fut.await;
}
```
You can also use `#[pollster::test]` for tests.

[§](https://docs.rs#comparison-with-futuresexecutorblock_on)Comparison with `futures::executor::block_on`

`pollster` does approximately the same thing as the `block_on` function from the `futures` crate. If you already have `futures` in your dependency tree, you might as well use it instead. `pollster` is primarily for applications that don’t care to pull all of `futures` or another runtime like `tokio` into their dependency tree for the sake of evaluating simple futures.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version-msrv-policy)Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) Policy

Current MSRV: `1.69.0`

`pollster` has a policy of supporting compiler versions that are at least 18 months old. The crate *may* compile with
older compilers, but this is not guaranteed.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Future](https://docs.rs/trait.FutureExt.html)- Ext
- An extension trait that allows blocking on a future in suffix position.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [block_](https://docs.rs/fn.block_on.html)- on
- Block the thread until the future is ready.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [main](https://docs.rs/attr.main.html)- `macro`
- Uses `pollster::block_on``async fn main() {}`.
- [test](https://docs.rs/attr.test.html)- `macro`
- Uses `pollster::block_on``async`on test functions.

# repose_text - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/repose-text/^0.21.0/

Look up the CacheKey for a GlyphKey and extract outline commands in one engine lock.
Returns None if the GlyphKey isn’t in the key map or extraction fails.

Like wrap_lines, but returns byte ranges into the original text
for each visual line. This is required for multi-line editing so
caret/selection mapping stays correct.

Greedy wrap into lines that fit max_width. Prefers breaking at whitespace,
falls back to grapheme boundaries. If max_lines is Some and we truncate,
caller can choose to ellipsize the last visible line.

# wgpu - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wgpu/^30/

## Expand description

`wgpu` is a cross-platform, safe, pure-Rust graphics API. It runs natively on
Vulkan, Metal, D3D12, and OpenGL; and on top of WebGL2 and WebGPU on wasm.

The API is based on the [WebGPU standard](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/), but is a fully native Rust library.
It serves as the core of the WebGPU integration in Firefox, Servo, and Deno.

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting Started

The main entry point to the API is the [ Instance](https://docs.rs/struct.Instance.html) type, from which you can create

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Adapter.html)

`Adapter`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Device.html)

`Device`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Surface.html)

`Surface`If you are new to `wgpu` and graphics programming, we recommend starting with [Learn Wgpu](https://sotrh.github.io/learn-wgpu/).

Additionally, [WebGPU Fundamentals](https://webgpufundamentals.org/) is a tutorial for WebGPU which is very similar to our API, minus differences between Rust and Javascript.

We have a [wiki](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/wiki) which has information on useful architecture patterns, debugging tips, and more getting started information.

There are examples for this version [available on GitHub](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/tree/v30/examples#readme).

The API is refcounted, so all handles are cloneable, and if you create a resource which references another, it will automatically keep dependent resources alive.

`wgpu` uses the coordinate systems of D3D and Metal. Depth ranges from [0, 1].

| Render | Texture |
|---|---|

`wgpu`’s MSRV is **1.87**.

[§](https://docs.rs#extension-specifications)Extension Specifications

While the core of `wgpu` is based on the WebGPU standard, we also support extensions that allow for features that the standard does not have yet.
For high-level documentation on how to use these extensions, see documentation on [ Features](https://docs.rs/struct.Features.html) or the relevant specification:

🧪EXPERIMENTAL🧪 APIs are subject to change and may allow undefined behavior if used incorrectly.

- 🧪EXPERIMENTAL🧪 [Ray Tracing](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/blob/v30/docs/api-specs/ray_tracing.md).
- 🧪EXPERIMENTAL🧪 [Mesh Shading](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/blob/v30/docs/api-specs/mesh_shading.md).

[§](https://docs.rs#shader-support)Shader Support

`wgpu` can consume shaders in [WGSL](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/wgsl/), SPIR-V, and GLSL.
Both [HLSL](https://github.com/Microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler) and [GLSL](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang)
have compilers to target SPIR-V. All of these shader languages can be used with any backend as we handle all of the conversions. Additionally, support for these shader inputs is not going away.

While WebGPU does not support any shading language other than WGSL, we will automatically convert your non-WGSL shaders if you’re running on WebGPU.

WGSL is always supported by default, but GLSL and SPIR-V need features enabled to compile in support.

To enable WGSL shaders, enable the `wgsl` feature of `wgpu` (enabled by default).
To enable SPIR-V shaders, enable the `spirv` feature of `wgpu`.
To enable GLSL shaders, enable the `glsl` feature of `wgpu`.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

- `metal`- *(enabled by default)*— Enables the Metal backend on macOS & iOS.
- `vulkan`- *(enabled by default)*— Enables the Vulkan backend on Windows, Linux, and Android.
- `gles`- *(enabled by default)*— Enables the OpenGL/GLES backend on Windows, Linux, Android, and Emscripten.

[§](https://docs.rs#surface-color-spaces-and-hdr-output)Surface color spaces and HDR output

A surface can present in different color spaces to get HDR or wide-gamut
output onto the screen. This is configured through
[ SurfaceConfiguration::color_space](https://docs.rs/type.SurfaceConfiguration.html#structfield.color_space), and the rest of this section is a
concept primer on how it works.

[§](https://docs.rs#hdr-output-in-a-nutshell)HDR output in a nutshell

By default a surface is standard dynamic range (SDR) with the sRGB gamut: the
value `1.0` is the brightest white, anything above it clips, and only colors
within sRGB are expressible. Other [ SurfaceColorSpace](https://docs.rs/enum.SurfaceColorSpace.html)s opt into a

**wider gamut**(for example

[, still SDR but with more saturated colors than sRGB),](https://docs.rs/enum.SurfaceColorSpace.html#variant.DisplayP3)

`DisplayP3`**high dynamic range**(values above

`1.0` drive brighter-than-white output), or both (for example
[, aka HDR10), on platforms that support it.](https://docs.rs/enum.SurfaceColorSpace.html#variant.Bt2100Pq)

`Bt2100Pq`Three ideas carry most of the weight:

- **Reference white and headroom.**Brightness is measured in- *nits*(cd/m²). On HDR-capable monitors, SDR reference white (plain white,- `(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)`in the extended color spaces) sits- *below*the display’s peak output on purpose, so highlights have room above it. That gap is the display’s- *headroom*.
- **The transfer function is a round-trip.**Your shader applies an encoding transfer function (the OETF) to turn the light it computed into a stored signal, and the display applies the inverse decoding transfer function (the EOTF) to turn it back into light. Choosing a color space chooses which transfer functions both ends use.
- **Who applies the encoding transfer function.**wgpu applies it for you- **only**when you render to an- `*Srgb`texture view format, where the GPU runs the sRGB OETF when a value is stored to a texture. For every other color space (linear extended sRGB, encoded extended sRGB or P3, PQ, HLG)- **the values your shader writes to the surface texture must already be encoded by you**, along with any gamut conversion; in a typical renderer this happens in a final tone-mapping or post-processing pass. wgpu hands the signal to the compositor unchanged; getting this wrong produces a wrong image with no error.

wgpu does **not** tonemap or gamut-map for you. It gives you the surface
and, through [ DisplayHdrInfo](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayHdrInfo.html), the display’s advisory capabilities;

*choosing*and

*applying*a tone curve is your application’s job.

[§](https://docs.rs#the-practical-path)The practical path

- **Query capabilities.**Call- `Surface::get_capabilities`. To use HDR or wide-gamut output, read- `SurfaceCapabilities::format_capabilities`- `SurfaceColorSpaces`- **not**- `SurfaceCapabilities::formats`- `Auto`- `SurfaceCapabilities::color_spaces`
- **Optionally query the display.**Call- `Surface::display_hdr_info`for the current- `DisplayHdrInfo`- `DisplayHdrInfo::tone_map_headroom`- *whether*HDR is worthwhile is the capability question from step 1, not this live value. Every field is advisory and optional;- `None`means “cannot tell here”, never “SDR”.
- **Choose a format and color space.**Intersect what you want with what step 1 advertises, in your own preference order (for example HDR10, then linear extended sRGB, then encoded extended sRGB, then SDR- `Srgb`
- **Configure the surface.**Set- `SurfaceConfiguration::color_space`- `format`.- `Auto`
- **Encode what you write to the surface texture.**For an- `*Srgb`format, output linear and the hardware encodes for you. Otherwise the values your shader writes to the surface texture must already carry the encoding the chosen color space expects (sRGB, extended sRGB, PQ, or HLG)- **and**any gamut conversion (for example outputting in the BT.2020 gamut for HDR10); in a typical renderer you do this in a final tone-mapping or post-processing pass. See the table below.
- **Present**as usual. If OS HDR is toggled mid-run, you’ll see it on the next- `Surface::display_hdr_info`poll; re-query- `Surface::get_capabilities`and re-run the steps above.

The standalone [HDR surface example](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/tree/v30/examples/standalone/03_hdr_surface) implements every step, including the
encoding transfer function for each color space.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-to-output-from-your-fragment-shader)What to output from your fragment shader

What the values your shader writes to the surface texture must contain for each color space, and whether wgpu applies the transfer function for you:

| Color space | Typical format | You write | wgpu encodes? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Srgb`,`*Srgb`format | `{Rgba,Bgra}8UnormSrgb` | linear | yes(hardware sRGB OETF on store) |
| `Srgb`, non-srgb format | `{Rgba,Bgra}8Unorm` | sRGB-encoded | no; apply the sRGB OETF yourself or use `*Srgb`instead |
| `ExtendedSrgbLinear`(scRGB) | `Rgba16Float` | linear, `1.0`= SDR white | no, but no encoding is necessary |
| `ExtendedSrgb` | `Rgba16Float` | extended sRGB-encoded | no; apply the extended sRGB OETF yourself |
| `DisplayP3` | `Bgra8Unorm` | sRGB-encoded, P3 primaries | no; apply the sRGB OETF (after gamut-mapping to P3) |
| `ExtendedDisplayP3` | `Rgba16Float` | extended sRGB-encoded, P3 primaries | no; apply the extended sRGB OETF (after gamut-mapping to P3) |
| `Bt2100Pq`(HDR10) | `Rgb10a2Unorm` | PQ-encoded, BT.2020 primaries | no; apply the PQ OETF (after gamut-mapping to BT.2020) |
| `Bt2100Hlg` | `Rgb10a2Unorm` | HLG-encoded, BT.2020 primaries | no; apply the HLG OETF (after gamut-mapping to BT.2020) |

In short, wgpu applies the transfer function for you only when you render to
an `*Srgb` format. In every other case the values your shader writes to the
surface texture must already carry both the transfer function and any gamut
conversion. The [HDR surface example](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/tree/v30/examples/standalone/03_hdr_surface) implements every encoder in WGSL.

[§](https://docs.rs#glossary)Glossary

- **Chromaticity**— a color’s hue and saturation independent of its brightness, given as an- `(x, y)`coordinate on the CIE 1931 diagram.
- **Primaries / gamut**— the chromaticities of the red, green, and blue a color space addresses, and so the range of colors it can express.- [BT.709](https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.709)is the sRGB gamut,- [Display P3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DCI-P3#Display_P3)is wider, and- [BT.2020](https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.2020)is wider still.
- **White point**— the chromaticity of- `R = G = B`(what “white” looks like). Every color space here uses- [D65](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_illuminant#D65_values), standard daylight.
- **Transfer function (OETF / EOTF)**— how stored values map to light. The- *OETF*is the encoding transfer function your application applies; the- *EOTF*is the inverse decoding transfer function the display applies.
- **SDR / HDR**— standard dynamic range clips at- `1.0`(reference white); high dynamic range lets values above- `1.0`drive brighter-than-white output.
- **Nits and reference white**— a- *nit*(cd/m²) is a unit of brightness;- *reference white*(also called- *paper white*, especially on Windows) is the brightness of SDR plain white, set below the panel’s peak so highlights have room above it.
- **Headroom (EDR)**— how much brighter than current SDR white the display can go right now, as a multiplier (- `1.0`means none). Dynamic; see- `DisplayHdrInfo::tone_map_headroom`
- **PQ / HLG**— the two HDR transfer functions:- [PQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptual_quantizer)(SMPTE ST 2084, HDR10) encodes absolute luminance,- [HLG](https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.2100)(BT.2100) encodes relative luminance.
- **scRGB / extended-range sRGB**— sRGB extended past 0.0..=1.0 for HDR:- [scRGB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ScRGB)is- *linear*(- `ExtendedSrgbLinear`- `ExtendedSrgb`- *encoded*(gamma), the web’s HDR path.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports-1)

- `pub use ::wgc::`- [naga](https://docs.rs/naga/30.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/naga/index.html);- `naga`or- `wgpu_core`
- `pub use`- [raw_window_handle](https://docs.rs/raw-window-handle/0.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/raw_window_handle/index.html)as rwh;

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [custom](https://docs.rs/custom/index.html)- `custom`
- Provides wrappers custom backend implementations
- [util](https://docs.rs/util/index.html)
- Utility structures and functions that are built on top of the main `wgpu`API.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [include_](https://docs.rs/macro.include_spirv.html)- spirv - `spirv`
- Macro to load a SPIR-V module statically.
- [include_](https://docs.rs/macro.include_spirv_raw.html)- spirv_ - raw
- Macro to load raw SPIR-V data statically, for use with `Features::PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS`
- [include_](https://docs.rs/macro.include_wgsl.html)- wgsl
- Load WGSL source code from a file at compile time.
- [vertex_](https://docs.rs/macro.vertex_attr_array.html)- attr_ - array
- Macro to produce an array of `VertexAttribute`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Adapter](https://docs.rs/struct.Adapter.html)
- Handle to a physical graphics and/or compute device.
- [Adapter](https://docs.rs/struct.AdapterInfo.html)- Info
- Information about an adapter.
- [Allocator](https://docs.rs/struct.AllocatorReport.html)- Report
- A report that can be generated for informational purposes using `Allocator::generate_report()`.
- [Backend](https://docs.rs/struct.BackendOptions.html)- Options
- Options that are passed to a given backend.
- [Backends](https://docs.rs/struct.Backends.html)
- Represents the backends that wgpu will use.
- [Bind](https://docs.rs/struct.BindGroup.html)- Group
- Handle to a binding group.
- [Bind](https://docs.rs/struct.BindGroupDescriptor.html)- Group - Descriptor
- Describes a group of bindings and the resources to be bound.
- [Bind](https://docs.rs/struct.BindGroupEntry.html)- Group - Entry
- An element of a `BindGroupDescriptor`
- [Bind](https://docs.rs/struct.BindGroupLayout.html)- Group - Layout
- Handle to a binding group layout.
- [Bind](https://docs.rs/struct.BindGroupLayoutDescriptor.html)- Group - Layout - Descriptor
- Describes a `BindGroupLayout`
- [Bind](https://docs.rs/struct.BindGroupLayoutEntry.html)- Group - Layout - Entry
- Describes a single binding inside a bind group.
- [Blas](https://docs.rs/struct.Blas.html)
- Bottom Level Acceleration Structure (BLAS).
- [Blas](https://docs.rs/struct.BlasAabbGeometry.html)- Aabb - Geometry
- Definition for an axis-aligned bounding box geometry group for a bottom level acceleration structure.
- [Blas](https://docs.rs/struct.BlasAsyncError.html)- Async - Error
- Error occurred when trying to asynchronously prepare a blas for compaction.
- [Blas](https://docs.rs/struct.BlasBuildEntry.html)- Build - Entry
- Builds the given sets of geometry into the given [Blas](https://docs.rs/struct.Blas.html).
- [Blas](https://docs.rs/struct.BlasTriangleGeometry.html)- Triangle - Geometry
- Definition for a triangle geometry for a Bottom Level Acceleration Structure (BLAS).
- [Blend](https://docs.rs/struct.BlendComponent.html)- Component
- Describes a blend component of a `BlendState`
- [Blend](https://docs.rs/struct.BlendState.html)- State
- Describe the blend state of a render pipeline,
within `ColorTargetState`
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.Buffer.html)
- Handle to a GPU-accessible buffer.
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferAsyncError.html)- Async - Error
- Error occurred when trying to async map a buffer.
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferBinding.html)- Binding
- Describes the segment of a buffer to bind.
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferSlice.html)- Slice
- A slice of a `Buffer`
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferTextureCopyInfo.html)- Texture - Copy - Info
- Information about a copy between a buffer and a texture.
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferTransition.html)- Transition
- A buffer transition for use with `CommandEncoder::transition_resources`.
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferUsages.html)- Usages
- Different ways that you can use a buffer.
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferUses.html)- Uses
- Similar to `BufferUsages`, but used only for`CommandEncoder::transition_resources`.
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferView.html)- View
- A read-only view of a mapped buffer’s bytes.
- [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.BufferViewMut.html)- View - Mut
- A write-only view of a mapped buffer’s bytes.
- [Color](https://docs.rs/struct.Color.html)
- RGBA double precision color.
- [Color](https://docs.rs/struct.ColorTargetState.html)- Target - State
- Describes the color state of a render pipeline.
- [Color](https://docs.rs/struct.ColorWrites.html)- Writes
- Color write mask. Disabled color channels will not be written to.
- [Command](https://docs.rs/struct.CommandBuffer.html)- Buffer
- Handle to a command buffer on the GPU.
- [Command](https://docs.rs/struct.CommandBufferDescriptor.html)- Buffer - Descriptor
- Describes a `CommandBuffer`
- [Command](https://docs.rs/struct.CommandEncoder.html)- Encoder
- Encodes a series of GPU operations.
- [Compilation](https://docs.rs/struct.CompilationInfo.html)- Info
- Compilation information for a shader module.
- [Compilation](https://docs.rs/struct.CompilationMessage.html)- Message
- A single message from the shader compilation process.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputePass.html)- Pass
- In-progress recording of a compute pass.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputePassDescriptor.html)- Pass - Descriptor
- Describes the attachments of a compute pass.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputePassTimestampWrites.html)- Pass - Timestamp - Writes
- Describes the timestamp writes of a compute pass.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputePipeline.html)- Pipeline
- Handle to a compute pipeline.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputePipelineDescriptor.html)- Pipeline - Descriptor
- Describes a compute pipeline.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextBlasAabbGeometry.html)- Blas - Aabb - Geometry
- Context version of [BlasAabbGeometry](https://docs.rs/struct.BlasAabbGeometry.html).
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextBlasBuildEntry.html)- Blas - Build - Entry
- Context version see [BlasBuildEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.BlasBuildEntry.html).
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.ContextBlasTriangleGeometry.html)- Blas - Triangle - Geometry
- Context version of [BlasTriangleGeometry](https://docs.rs/struct.BlasTriangleGeometry.html).
- [Cooperative](https://docs.rs/struct.CooperativeMatrixProperties.html)- Matrix - Properties
- Describes a supported cooperative matrix configuration.
- [Copy](https://docs.rs/struct.CopyExternalImageDestInfo.html)- External - Image - Dest - Info
- View of a texture which can be used to copy to a texture, including color space and alpha premultiplication information.
- [Core](https://docs.rs/struct.CoreCounters.html)- Counters
- `wgpu-core`’s part of- `InternalCounters`
- [Create](https://docs.rs/struct.CreateSurfaceError.html)- Surface - Error
- `Instance::create_surface()`
- [Depth](https://docs.rs/struct.DepthBiasState.html)- Bias - State
- Describes the biasing setting for the depth target.
- [Depth](https://docs.rs/struct.DepthStencilState.html)- Stencil - State
- Describes the depth/stencil state in a render pipeline.
- [Device](https://docs.rs/struct.Device.html)
- Open connection to a graphics and/or compute device.
- [Display](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayChromaticity.html)- Chromaticity
- CIE 1931 xy chromaticity of a display’s primaries and white point. Each
coordinate is `[x, y]`; a coordinate the platform omits is`None`.
- [Display](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayCoarseRange.html)- Coarse - Range
- Coarse, boolean dynamic-range and gamut signal.
- [Display](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayHdrInfo.html)- HdrInfo
- HDR and luminance characteristics of the display backing a `Surface`
- [Display](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayHeadroom.html)- Headroom
- Relative EDR headroom (Apple): unitless multipliers over current SDR white,
where `1.0`means no headroom. Moves with brightness, ambient light, battery, and which display the window is on. Apple exposes no absolute-nit equivalent, so this is separate from`DisplayLuminance`
- [Display](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayLuminance.html)- Luminance
- Absolute luminance levels in nits (cd/m²). Populated only on Windows (via
DXGI); `None`on every other platform.
- [Downlevel](https://docs.rs/struct.DownlevelCapabilities.html)- Capabilities
- Lists various ways the underlying platform does not conform to the WebGPU standard.
- [Downlevel](https://docs.rs/struct.DownlevelFlags.html)- Flags
- Binary flags listing features that may or may not be present on downlevel adapters.
- [Downlevel](https://docs.rs/struct.DownlevelLimits.html)- Limits
- Represents the sets of additional limits on an adapter, which take place when running on downlevel backends.
- [Dx12](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx12BackendOptions.html)- Backend - Options
- Configuration for the DX12 backend.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.ErrorScopeGuard.html)- Scope - Guard
- Guard for an error scope pushed with `Device::push_error_scope()`
- [Experimental](https://docs.rs/struct.ExperimentalFeatures.html)- Features
- Token of the user agreeing to access experimental features.
- [Extent3d](https://docs.rs/struct.Extent3d.html)
- Extent of a texture related operation.
- [External](https://docs.rs/struct.ExternalTexture.html)- Texture
- Handle to an external texture on the GPU.
- [External](https://docs.rs/struct.ExternalTextureTransferFunction.html)- Texture - Transfer - Function
- Parameters describing a gamma encoding transfer function in the form tf = { k * linear | linear < b { a * pow(linear, 1/g) - (a-1) | linear >= b
- [Features](https://docs.rs/struct.Features.html)
- Features that are not guaranteed to be supported.
- [FeaturesWGPU](https://docs.rs/struct.FeaturesWGPU.html)
- Features that are not guaranteed to be supported.
- [Features](https://docs.rs/struct.FeaturesWebGPU.html)- WebGPU
- Features that are not guaranteed to be supported.
- [Force](https://docs.rs/struct.ForceShaderModelToken.html)- Shader - Model - Token
- Used to force wgpu to expose certain features on passthrough shaders even when those features aren’t present on runtime-compiled shaders
- [Fragment](https://docs.rs/struct.FragmentState.html)- State

- [GlBackend](https://docs.rs/struct.GlBackendOptions.html)- Options

- [HalCounters](https://docs.rs/struct.HalCounters.html)

- [Image](https://docs.rs/struct.ImageSubresourceRange.html)- Subresource - Range
