# winit - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/winit/^0.30/

## Expand description

Winit is a cross-platform window creation and event loop management library.

[§](https://docs.rs#building-windows)Building windows

Before you can create a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html), you first need to build an

[. This is done with the](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html)

`EventLoop`[function.](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html#method.new)

`EventLoop::new()````
use winit::event_loop::EventLoop;
fn main() {
    let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
    // ...
}
```
Then you create a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html) with

[.](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.ActiveEventLoop.html#method.create_window)

`create_window`[§](https://docs.rs#event-handling)Event handling

Once a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html) has been created, it will generate different

*events*. A

[object can generate](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[s when certain input events occur, such as a cursor moving over the window or a key getting pressed while the window is focused. Devices can generate](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html)

`WindowEvent`[s, which contain unfiltered event data that isn’t specific to a certain window. Some user activity, like mouse movement, can generate both a](https://docs.rs/event/enum.DeviceEvent.html)

`DeviceEvent`

`WindowEvent`*and*a

[. You can also create and handle your own custom](https://docs.rs/event/enum.DeviceEvent.html)

`DeviceEvent`[s, if desired.](https://docs.rs/event/enum.Event.html#variant.UserEvent)

`Event::UserEvent`You can retrieve events by calling [ EventLoop::run_app()](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html#method.run_app). This function will
dispatch events for every

[that was created with that particular](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[, and will run until](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html)

`EventLoop`[is used, at which point](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.ActiveEventLoop.html#method.exit)

`exit()`[.](https://docs.rs/event/enum.Event.html#variant.LoopExiting)

`Event::LoopExiting`Winit no longer uses a `EventLoop::poll_events() -> impl Iterator<Event>`-based event loop
model, since that can’t be implemented properly on some platforms (e.g web, iOS) and works
poorly on most other platforms. However, this model can be re-implemented to an extent with
`EventLoopExtPumpEvents::pump_app_events()` 1. See that method’s documentation for more reasons about why
it’s discouraged beyond compatibility reasons.

```
use winit::application::ApplicationHandler;
use winit::event::WindowEvent;
use winit::event_loop::{ActiveEventLoop, ControlFlow, EventLoop};
use winit::window::{Window, WindowId};
#[derive(Default)]
struct App {
    window: Option<Window>,
}
impl ApplicationHandler for App {
    fn resumed(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop) {
        self.window = Some(event_loop.create_window(Window::default_attributes()).unwrap());
    }
    fn window_event(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop, id: WindowId, event: WindowEvent) {
        match event {
            WindowEvent::CloseRequested => {
                println!("The close button was pressed; stopping");
                event_loop.exit();
            },
            WindowEvent::RedrawRequested => {
                // Redraw the application.
                //
                // It's preferable for applications that do not render continuously to render in
                // this event rather than in AboutToWait, since rendering in here allows
                // the program to gracefully handle redraws requested by the OS.
                // Draw.
                // Queue a RedrawRequested event.
                //
                // You only need to call this if you've determined that you need to redraw in
                // applications which do not always need to. Applications that redraw continuously
                // can render here instead.
                self.window.as_ref().unwrap().request_redraw();
            }
            _ => (),
        }
    }
}
fn main() {
    let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
    // ControlFlow::Poll continuously runs the event loop, even if the OS hasn't
    // dispatched any events. This is ideal for games and similar applications.
    event_loop.set_control_flow(ControlFlow::Poll);
    // ControlFlow::Wait pauses the event loop if no events are available to process.
    // This is ideal for non-game applications that only update in response to user
    // input, and uses significantly less power/CPU time than ControlFlow::Poll.
    event_loop.set_control_flow(ControlFlow::Wait);
    let mut app = App::default();
    event_loop.run_app(&mut app);
}
```
[ WindowEvent](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html) has a

[member. In multi-window environments, it should be compared to the value returned by](https://docs.rs/window/struct.WindowId.html)

`WindowId`[to determine which](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.id)

`Window::id()`[dispatched the event.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[§](https://docs.rs#drawing-on-the-window)Drawing on the window

Winit doesn’t directly provide any methods for drawing on a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html). However, it allows you
to retrieve the raw handle of the window and display (see the

[module and/or the](https://docs.rs/platform/index.html)

`platform`[and](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.raw_window_handle)

`raw_window_handle`[methods), which in turn allows you to create an OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX/Metal/etc. context that can be used to render graphics.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.raw_display_handle)

`raw_display_handle`Note that many platforms will display garbage data in the window’s client area if the
application doesn’t render anything to the window by the time the desktop compositor is ready to
display the window to the user. If you notice this happening, you should create the window with
[ visible set to false](https://docs.rs/window/struct.WindowAttributes.html#method.with_visible) and explicitly make
the window visible only once you’re ready to render into it.

[§](https://docs.rs#ui-scaling)UI scaling

UI scaling is important, go read the docs for the [ dpi](https://docs.rs/dpi/index.html) crate for an
introduction.

All of Winit’s functions return physical types, but can take either logical or physical coordinates as input, allowing you to use the most convenient coordinate system for your particular application.

Winit will dispatch a [ ScaleFactorChanged](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html#variant.ScaleFactorChanged) event whenever a window’s scale factor has changed.
This can happen if the user drags their window from a standard-resolution monitor to a high-DPI
monitor or if the user changes their DPI settings. This allows you to rescale your application’s
UI elements and adjust how the platform changes the window’s size to reflect the new scale
factor. If a window hasn’t received a

[event, its scale factor can be found by calling](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html#variant.ScaleFactorChanged)

`ScaleFactorChanged`[.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.scale_factor)

`window.scale_factor()`[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-features)Cargo Features

Winit provides the following Cargo features:

- `x11`(enabled by default): On Unix platforms, enables the X11 backend.
- `wayland`(enabled by default): On Unix platforms, enables the Wayland backend.
- `rwh_04`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.4`traits.
- `rwh_05`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.5`traits.
- `rwh_06`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.6`traits.
- `serde`: Enables serialization/deserialization of certain types with- [Serde](https://crates.io/crates/serde).
- `mint`: Enables mint (math interoperability standard types) conversions.

See the [ platform](https://docs.rs/platform/index.html) module for documentation on platform-specific cargo
features.

[15](#15)struct UploadRing {
[16](#16)    buf: wgpu::Buffer,
[17](#17)    cap: u64,
[18](#18)    head: u64,
[19](#19)}
[20](#20)
[21](#21)impl UploadRing {
[22](#22)    fn new(device: &wgpu::Device, label: &str, cap: u64) -> Self {
[23](#23)        let buf = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
[24](#24)            label: Some(label),
[25](#25)            size: cap,
[26](#26)            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::VERTEX | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
[27](#27)            mapped_at_creation: false,
[28](#28)        });
[29](#29)        Self { buf, cap, head: 0 }
[30](#30)    }
[31](#31)
[32](#32)    fn reset(&mut self) {
[33](#33)        self.head = 0;
[34](#34)    }
[35](#35)
[36](#36)    fn grow_to_fit(&mut self, device: &wgpu::Device, needed: u64) {
[37](#37)        let start = (self.head + 3) & !3;
[38](#38)        if start + needed <= self.cap {
[39](#39)            return;
[40](#40)        }
[41](#41)        let new_cap = (start + needed).next_power_of_two();
[42](#42)        self.buf = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
[43](#43)            label: Some("upload ring (grown)"),
[44](#44)            size: new_cap,
[45](#45)            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::VERTEX | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
[46](#46)            mapped_at_creation: false,
[47](#47)        });
[48](#48)        self.cap = new_cap;
[49](#49)    }
[50](#50)
[51](#51)    fn alloc_write(&mut self, queue: &wgpu::Queue, bytes: &[u8]) -> (u64, u64) {
[52](#52)        let len = bytes.len() as u64;
[53](#53)        let start = (self.head + 3) & !3; let end = start + len;
[55](#55)        assert!(end <= self.cap, "ring overflow - call grow_to_fit first");
[56](#56)        queue.write_buffer(&self.buf, start, bytes);
[57](#57)        self.head = end;
[58](#58)        (start, len)
[59](#59)    }
[60](#60)}

[62](#62)struct InstancedPipe<I: bytemuck::Pod> {
[63](#63)    ring: UploadRing,
[64](#64)    _marker: std::marker::PhantomData<I>,
[65](#65)}
[66](#66)
[67](#67)impl<I: bytemuck::Pod> InstancedPipe<I> {
[68](#68)    fn new(ring: UploadRing) -> Self {
[69](#69)        Self {
[70](#70)            ring,
[71](#71)            _marker: std::marker::PhantomData,
[72](#72)        }
[73](#73)    }
[74](#74)
[75](#75)    fn upload(
[76](#76)        &mut self,
[77](#77)        device: &wgpu::Device,
[78](#78)        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
[79](#79)        data: &[I],
[80](#80)    ) -> Option<(u64, u32)> {
[81](#81)        if data.is_empty() {
[82](#82)            return None;
[83](#83)        }
[84](#84)        let bytes = bytemuck::cast_slice(data);
[85](#85)        self.ring.grow_to_fit(device, bytes.len() as u64);
[86](#86)        let (off, wrote) = self.ring.alloc_write(queue, bytes);
[87](#87)        debug_assert_eq!(wrote as usize, bytes.len());
[88](#88)        Some((off, data.len() as u32))
[89](#89)    }
[90](#90)
[91](#91)    fn reset(&mut self) {
[92](#92)        self.ring.reset();
[93](#93)    }

[1117](#1117)fn swash_to_a8_coverage(content: cosmic_text::SwashContent, data: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
[1118](#1118)    match content {
[1119](#1119)        cosmic_text::SwashContent::Mask => Some(data.to_vec()),
[1120](#1120)        cosmic_text::SwashContent::SubpixelMask => {
[1121](#1121)            let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(data.len() / 4);
[1122](#1122)            for px in data.chunks_exact(4) {
[1123](#1123)                let r = px[0];
[1124](#1124)                let g = px[1];
[1125](#1125)                let b = px[2];
[1126](#1126)                out.push(r.max(g).max(b));
[1127](#1127)            }
[1128](#1128)            Some(out)
[1129](#1129)        }
[1130](#1130)        cosmic_text::SwashContent::Color => None,
[1131](#1131)    }
[1132](#1132)}

[1874](#1874)    fn evict_unused_images(&mut self) {
[1875](#1875)        let now = self.frame_index;
[1876](#1876)        let evict_after = self.image_evict_after_frames;
[1877](#1877)
[1878](#1878)        let mut to_remove = Vec::new();
[1880](#1880)        for (h, t) in self.images.iter() {
[1881](#1881)            let last = match t {
[1882](#1882)                ImageTex::Rgba {
[1883](#1883)                    last_used_frame, ..
[1884](#1884)                } => *last_used_frame,
[1885](#1885)                ImageTex::Nv12 {
[1886](#1886)                    last_used_frame, ..
[1887](#1887)                } => *last_used_frame,
[1888](#1888)            };
[1889](#1889)            if now.saturating_sub(last) > evict_after {
[1890](#1890)                to_remove.push(*h);
[1891](#1891)            }
[1892](#1892)        }
[1893](#1893)        for h in to_remove {
[1894](#1894)            self.remove_image(h);
[1895](#1895)        }
[1896](#1896)
[1897](#1897)        self.evict_budget_excess();
[1898](#1898)    }
[1899](#1899)
[1900](#1900)    fn evict_budget_excess(&mut self) {
[1901](#1901)        if self.image_bytes_total <= self.image_budget_bytes {
[1902](#1902)            return;
[1903](#1903)        }
[1904](#1904)        let mut candidates: Vec<(u64, u64, u64)> = self
[1906](#1906)            .images
[1907](#1907)            .iter()
[1908](#1908)            .map(|(h, t)| {
[1909](#1909)                let (last, bytes) = match t {
[1910](#1910)                    ImageTex::Rgba {
[1911](#1911)                        last_used_frame,
[1912](#1912)                        bytes,
[1913](#1913)                        ..
[1914](#1914)                    } => (*last_used_frame, *bytes),
[1915](#1915)                    ImageTex::Nv12 {
[1916](#1916)                        last_used_frame,
[1917](#1917)                        bytes,
[1918](#1918)                        ..
[1919](#1919)                    } => (*last_used_frame, *bytes),
[1920](#1920)                };
[1921](#1921)                (*h, last, bytes)
[1922](#1922)            })
[1923](#1923)            .collect();
[1924](#1924)
[1925](#1925)        candidates.sort_by_key(|k| k.1);
[1927](#1927)
[1928](#1928)        let now = self.frame_index;

[1931](#1931)                break;
[1932](#1932)            }
[1933](#1933)            if last == now {
[1935](#1935)                continue;
[1936](#1936)            }
[1937](#1937)            self.remove_image(h);
[1938](#1938)        }
[1939](#1939)    }

[2171](#2171)    fn upload_glyph_mask(&mut self, key: repose_text::GlyphKey, px: u32) -> Option<GlyphInfo> {
[2172](#2172)        let keyp = (key, px);
[2173](#2173)        if let Some(info) = self.atlas_mask.map.get(&keyp) {
[2174](#2174)            return Some(*info);
[2175](#2175)        }
[2176](#2176)
[2177](#2177)        let gb = repose_text::rasterize(key, px as f32)?;
[2178](#2178)        if gb.w == 0 || gb.h == 0 || gb.data.is_empty() {
[2179](#2179)            return None;
[2180](#2180)        }
[2181](#2181)
[2182](#2182)        let coverage = swash_to_a8_coverage(gb.content, &gb.data)?;
[2183](#2183)
[2184](#2184)        let w = gb.w.max(1);
[2185](#2185)        let h = gb.h.max(1);
[2186](#2186)
[2187](#2187)        if !self.alloc_space_mask(w, h) {
[2188](#2188)            self.grow_mask_and_rebuild();
[2189](#2189)        }
[2190](#2190)        if !self.alloc_space_mask(w, h) {
[2191](#2191)            return None;
[2192](#2192)        }
[2193](#2193)        let x = self.atlas_mask.next_x;
[2194](#2194)        let y = self.atlas_mask.next_y;
[2195](#2195)        self.atlas_mask.next_x += w + 1;
[2196](#2196)        self.atlas_mask.row_h = self.atlas_mask.row_h.max(h + 1);
[2197](#2197)
[2198](#2198)        let layout = wgpu::TexelCopyBufferLayout {
[2199](#2199)            offset: 0,
[2200](#2200)            bytes_per_row: Some(w),
[2201](#2201)            rows_per_image: Some(h),
[2202](#2202)        };
[2203](#2203)        let size = wgpu::Extent3d {
[2204](#2204)            width: w,
[2205](#2205)            height: h,
[2206](#2206)            depth_or_array_layers: 1,
[2207](#2207)        };
[2208](#2208)        self.queue.write_texture(
[2209](#2209)            wgpu::TexelCopyTextureInfoBase {
[2210](#2210)                texture: &self.atlas_mask.tex,
[2211](#2211)                mip_level: 0,
[2212](#2212)                origin: wgpu::Origin3d { x, y, z: 0 },
[2213](#2213)                aspect: wgpu::TextureAspect::All,
[2214](#2214)            },
[2215](#2215)            &coverage,
[2216](#2216)            layout,
[2217](#2217)            size,
[2218](#2218)        );
[2219](#2219)
[2220](#2220)        let info = GlyphInfo {
[2221](#2221)            u0: x as f32 / self.atlas_mask.size as f32,
[2222](#2222)            v0: y as f32 / self.atlas_mask.size as f32,
[2223](#2223)            u1: (x + w) as f32 / self.atlas_mask.size as f32,
[2224](#2224)            v1: (y + h) as f32 / self.atlas_mask.size as f32,
[2225](#2225)            w: w as f32,
[2226](#2226)            h: h as f32,
[2227](#2227)            bearing_x: 0.0,
[2228](#2228)            bearing_y: 0.0,
[2229](#2229)            advance: 0.0,
[2230](#2230)        };
[2231](#2231)        self.atlas_mask.map.insert(keyp, info);
[2232](#2232)        Some(info)
[2233](#2233)    }

[2389](#2389)fn brush_to_instance_fields(brush: &Brush) -> (u32, [f32; 4], [f32; 4], [f32; 2], [f32; 2]) {

[2433](#2433)    fn frame(&mut self, scene: &Scene, _glyph_cfg: GlyphRasterConfig) {
[2434](#2434)        self.frame_index = self.frame_index.wrapping_add(1);
[2436](#2436)        self.slug_cache.next_frame();
[2437](#2437)
[2438](#2438)        if self.config.width == 0 || self.config.height == 0 {
[2439](#2439)            return;
[2440](#2440)        }
[2441](#2441)        let mut retries = 0u32;
[2442](#2442)        const MAX_RETRIES: u32 = 4;
[2443](#2443)        let frame = loop {
[2444](#2444)            match self.surface.get_current_texture() {
[2445](#2445)                wgpu::CurrentSurfaceTexture::Success(f) => break f,
[2446](#2446)                wgpu::CurrentSurfaceTexture::Suboptimal(f) => {
[2447](#2447)                    log::warn!("suboptimal surface; reconfiguring");
[2448](#2448)                    self.surface.configure(&self.device, &self.config);
[2449](#2449)                    break f;
[2450](#2450)                }
[2451](#2451)                wgpu::CurrentSurfaceTexture::Outdated => {
[2452](#2452)                    retries += 1;
[2453](#2453)                    if retries >= MAX_RETRIES {
[2454](#2454)                        log::warn!(
[2455](#2455)                            "surface outdated persisted after {MAX_RETRIES} retries; skipping frame"
[2456](#2456)                        );
[2457](#2457)                        return;
[2458](#2458)                    }
[2459](#2459)                    log::warn!("surface outdated; reconfiguring");
[2460](#2460)                    self.surface.configure(&self.device, &self.config);
[2461](#2461)                }
[2462](#2462)                wgpu::CurrentSurfaceTexture::Lost => {
[2463](#2463)                    retries += 1;
[2464](#2464)                    if retries >= MAX_RETRIES {
[2465](#2465)                        log::warn!(
[2466](#2466)                            "surface lost persisted after {MAX_RETRIES} retries; skipping frame"
[2467](#2467)                        );
[2468](#2468)                        return;
[2469](#2469)                    }
[2470](#2470)                    log::warn!("surface lost; reconfiguring");
[2471](#2471)                    self.surface.configure(&self.device, &self.config);
[2472](#2472)                }
[2473](#2473)                wgpu::CurrentSurfaceTexture::Timeout | wgpu::CurrentSurfaceTexture::Occluded => {
[2474](#2474)                    request_frame();
[2475](#2475)                    return;
[2476](#2476)                }
[2477](#2477)                wgpu::CurrentSurfaceTexture::Validation => {
[2478](#2478)                    retries += 1;
[2479](#2479)                    if retries >= MAX_RETRIES {
[2480](#2480)                        log::warn!(
[2481](#2481)                            "surface validation persisted after {MAX_RETRIES} retries; skipping frame"
[2482](#2482)                        );
[2483](#2483)                        return;
[2484](#2484)                    }
[2485](#2485)                    self.surface.configure(&self.device, &self.config);
[2486](#2486)                }
[2487](#2487)            }
[2488](#2488)        };

[2490](#2490)        fn to_ndc(x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32, fb_w: f32, fb_h: f32) -> [f32; 4] {
[2491](#2491)            let x0 = (x / fb_w) * 2.0 - 1.0;
[2492](#2492)            let y0 = 1.0 - (y / fb_h) * 2.0;
[2493](#2493)            let x1 = ((x + w) / fb_w) * 2.0 - 1.0;
[2494](#2494)            let y1 = 1.0 - ((y + h) / fb_h) * 2.0;
[2495](#2495)            let min_x = x0.min(x1);
[2496](#2496)            let min_y = y0.min(y1);
[2497](#2497)            let w_ndc = (x1 - x0).abs();
[2498](#2498)            let h_ndc = (y1 - y0).abs();
[2499](#2499)            [min_x, min_y, w_ndc, h_ndc]
[2500](#2500)        }
[2501](#2501)
[2502](#2502)        fn rect_to_instance_ndc(
[2504](#2504)            rect: repose_core::Rect,
[2505](#2505)            transform: &Transform,
[2506](#2506)            fb_w: f32,
[2507](#2507)            fb_h: f32,
[2508](#2508)        ) -> ([f32; 4], [f32; 2]) {
[2509](#2509)            let cx = rect.x + rect.w * 0.5;
[2510](#2510)            let cy = rect.y + rect.h * 0.5;
[2511](#2511)
[2512](#2512)            let sx = cx * transform.scale_x;
[2514](#2514)            let sy = cy * transform.scale_y;
[2515](#2515)            let cos_a = transform.rotate.cos();
[2516](#2516)            let sin_a = transform.rotate.sin();
[2517](#2517)            let tx = sx * cos_a - sy * sin_a + transform.translate_x;
[2518](#2518)            let ty = sx * sin_a + sy * cos_a + transform.translate_y;
[2519](#2519)
[2520](#2520)            let ndc_cx = (tx / fb_w) * 2.0 - 1.0;
[2522](#2522)            let ndc_cy = 1.0 - (ty / fb_h) * 2.0;
[2523](#2523)            let ndc_w = (rect.w * transform.scale_x / fb_w) * 2.0;
[2525](#2525)            let ndc_h = (rect.h * transform.scale_y / fb_h) * 2.0;
[2526](#2526)
[2527](#2527)            ([ndc_cx, ndc_cy, ndc_w, ndc_h], [cos_a, sin_a])
[2528](#2528)        }

[2530](#2530)        fn to_scissor(r: &repose_core::Rect, fb_w: u32, fb_h: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32, u32) {
[2531](#2531)            let mut x = r.x.floor() as i64;
[2532](#2532)            let mut y = r.y.floor() as i64;
[2533](#2533)            let fb_wi = fb_w as i64;
[2534](#2534)            let fb_hi = fb_h as i64;
[2535](#2535)            x = x.clamp(0, fb_wi.saturating_sub(1));
[2536](#2536)            y = y.clamp(0, fb_hi.saturating_sub(1));
[2537](#2537)            let w_req = r.w.ceil().max(1.0) as i64;
[2538](#2538)            let h_req = r.h.ceil().max(1.0) as i64;
[2539](#2539)            let w = (w_req).min(fb_wi - x).max(1);
[2540](#2540)            let h = (h_req).min(fb_hi - y).max(1);
[2541](#2541)            (x as u32, y as u32, w as u32, h as u32)
[2542](#2542)        }

# repose-ui 0.21.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/repose-ui/0.21.1

# Views, Modifiers, and Layout

Repose UI is built around three core ideas:

- `View`: an immutable description of a UI node.
- `Modifier`: layout, styling, and interaction hints attached to a- `View`.
- Layout + paint: a separate pass (`layout_and_paint`) that turns the`View`tree into a`Scene`+ hit regions using the Taffy layout engine.

## Views

A `View` is a lightweight value that describes *what* to show, not *how* it is
rendered. It is cheap to create and you are expected to rebuild the entire
view tree on each frame:

```
use *;
use *;
```
Internally, a `View` has:

- `id: ViewId`- assigned during composition/layout.
- `kind: ViewKind`- which widget it is (Text, Button, ScrollV, etc.).
- `modifier: Modifier`- layout/styling/interaction metadata.
- `children: Vec<View>`- owned child views.

Views are *pure data*: they do not hold state or references into platform
APIs. State lives in signals / `remember_*` and platform integration happens
in the runner (`repose-platform`).

## Modifiers

`Modifier` describes *how* a view participates in layout and hit‑testing:

- Size hints: `size`,`width`,`height`,`min_size`,`max_size`,`fill_max_size`,`fill_max_width`,`fill_max_height`.
- Box model: `padding`,`padding_values`.
- Visuals: `background`,`background_brush`,`border`,`clip_rounded`,`alpha`,`transform`.
- Flex / grid: `flex_grow`,`flex_shrink`,`flex_basis`,`align_self`,`justify_content`,`align_items`,`grid`,`grid_span`.
- Positioning: `absolute()`,`offset(..)`for overlay / Stack / FABs.
- Interaction: `clickable()`, pointer callbacks,`on_scroll`,`semantics`.
- Custom paint: `painter`(used by`repose-canvas`).

Example:

```
use *;
use *;
```
Modifiers are merged into a Taffy `Style` inside `layout_and_paint`. Most
values are specified in density‑independent pixels (dp) and converted to
physical pixels (`px`) using the current `Density` local.

## Layout

Layout is a pure function:

```
;
```
It:

- Clones the root `View`and assigns stable`ViewId`s.
- Builds a parallel Taffy tree and computes layout for the given window size.
- Walks the tree to:
- Emit `SceneNode`s for visuals (rects, text, images, scrollbars, etc.).
- Build `HitRegion`s for input routing (clicks, pointer events, scroll).
- Build `SemNode`s for accessibility / semantics.

- Emit

`Row`, `Column`, `Stack`, `Grid`, `ScrollV` and `ScrollXY` are all special
`ViewKind`s that map into Taffy styles and additional paint/hit logic.

Because layout + paint are separate from the platform runner, you can reuse the same UI code on desktop, Android, and other platforms.

# repose_tree - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/repose-tree/^0.21.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#repose-tree)repose-tree

Persistent view tree with incremental reconciliation.

Instead of rebuilding the entire view tree every frame, this module maintains a persistent tree structure that:

- **Stable Identity**: Nodes have stable IDs across frames
- **Change Detection**: Content hashing identifies what changed
- **Incremental Updates**: Only changed subtrees are processed
- **Layout Caching**: Unchanged nodes keep their cached layout

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ViewTree │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│ │ nodes: SlotMap<NodeId, TreeNode> ││
│ │ root: NodeId ││
│ │ dirty: FxHashSet<NodeId> ││
│ │ generation: u64 ││
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│
▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ TreeNode │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│ │ id: NodeId ││
│ │ view_id: ViewId (stable user-facing ID) ││
│ │ kind: ViewKind ││
│ │ modifier: Modifier ││
│ │ children: SmallVec<[NodeId; 4]> ││
│ │ parent: Option<NodeId> ││
│ │ content_hash: u64 ││
│ │ layout_cache: Option<LayoutCache> ││
│ │ generation: u64 ││
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- Cached layout information for a node.
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.LayoutConstraints.html)- Constraints
- Constraints used during layout.
- [NodeId](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeId.html)
- Internal node identifier, stable within a tree’s lifetime.
- [Reconcile](https://docs.rs/struct.ReconcileContext.html)- Context
- Context for a reconciliation pass.
- [Tree](https://docs.rs/struct.TreeNode.html)- Node
- A node in the persistent view tree.
- [Tree](https://docs.rs/struct.TreeStats.html)- Stats
- Statistics about tree operations.
- [View](https://docs.rs/struct.ViewTree.html)- Tree
- A persistent view tree that supports incremental updates.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_subtree.html)- subtree
- Compute a hash that includes the subtree structure. This combines the node’s content hash with its children’s subtree hashes.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_view_content.html)- view_ - content

"Small vector" optimization for Rust: store up to a small number of items on the stack

use ;

# taffy - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/taffy/^0.11/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#taffy)Taffy

Taffy is a flexible, high-performance library for **UI layout**.
It currently implements the Flexbox, Grid and Block layout algorithms from the CSS specification. Support for other paradigms is planned.
For more information on this and other future development plans see the [roadmap issue](https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/issues/345).

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

Taffy is based on a tree of “UI nodes” similar to the tree of DOM nodes that one finds in web-based UI. Each node has:

- A `Style`
- A `Layout`
- Optionally:
- A `Vec`set of child nodes
- “Context”: arbitrary user-defined data (which you can access when using a “measure function” to integrate Taffy with other kinds of layout such as text layout)

- A

Usage of Taffy consists of constructing a tree of UI nodes (with associated styles, children and context), then calling function(s) from Taffy to translate those styles, parent-child relationships and measure functions into a size and position in 2d space for each node in the tree.

[§](https://docs.rs#high-level-api-vs-low-level-api)High-level API vs. Low-level API

Taffy has two APIs: a high-level API that is simpler and easier to get started with, and a low-level API that is more flexible gives greater control. We would generally recommend the high-level API for users using Taffy standalone and the low-level API for users wanting to embed Taffy as part of a wider layout system or as part of a UI framework that already has it’s own node/widget tree representation.

[§](https://docs.rs#high-level-api)High-level API

The high-level API consists of the [ TaffyTree](https://docs.rs/struct.TaffyTree.html) struct which contains a tree implementation and provides methods that allow you to construct
a tree of UI nodes. Once constructed, you can call the

[method to compute the layout (passing in a “measure function” closure which is used to compute the size of leaf nodes), and then access the layout of each node using the](https://docs.rs/struct.TaffyTree.html#method.compute_layout_with_measure)

`compute_layout_with_measure`[method.](https://docs.rs/struct.TaffyTree.html#method.layout)

`layout`When using the high-level API, Taffy will take care of node storage, caching and dispatching to the correct layout algorithm for a given node for you.
See the [ TaffyTree](https://docs.rs/struct.TaffyTree.html) struct for more details on this API.

Examples which show usage of the high-level API include:

In particular, the “measure” example shows how to integrate Taffy layout with other layout modalities such as text or image layout when using the high level API.

[§](https://docs.rs#low-level-api)Low-level API

The low-level API consists of a [set of traits](https://docs.rs/tree/traits/index.html) (notably the [ LayoutPartialTree](https://docs.rs/trait.LayoutPartialTree.html) trait) which define an interface behind which you must implement your own
tree implementation, and a

[set of functions](https://docs.rs/compute/index.html)such as

[and](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_flexbox_layout.html)

`compute_flexbox_layout`[which implement the layout algorithms (for a single node at a time), and are designed to be flexible and easy to integrate into a wider layout or UI system.](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_grid_layout.html)

`compute_grid_layout`When using this API, you must handle node storage, caching, and dispatching to the correct layout algorithm for a given node yourself.
See the [ crate::tree::traits](https://docs.rs/tree/traits/index.html) module for more details on this API.

Examples which show usage of the low-level API are:

- [custom_tree_vec](https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/blob/main/examples/custom_tree_vec.rs)which implements a custom Taffy tree using a- `Vec`as an arena with NodeId’s being index’s into the Vec.
- [custom_tree_owned_partial](https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/blob/main/examples/custom_tree_owned_partial.rs)which implements a custom Taffy tree using directly owned children with NodeId’s being index’s into vec on parent node.
- [custom_tree_owned_unsafe](https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/blob/main/examples/custom_tree_owned_unsafe.rs)which implements a custom Taffy tree using directly owned children with NodeId’s being pointers.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

[§](https://docs.rs#algorithms)Algorithms

- `block_layout`- *(enabled by default)*— Enables the Block layout algorithm. See- `compute_block_layout`
- `float_layout`- *(enabled by default)*— Enables the Float layout algorithm. This is a sub-feature of block layout.
- `flexbox`- *(enabled by default)*— Enables the Flexbox layout algorithm. See- `compute_flexbox_layout`
- `grid`- *(enabled by default)*— Enables the CSS Grid layout algorithm. See- `compute_grid_layout`
- `calc`- *(enabled by default)*— Enables calc() values for all layout algorithms
- `content_size`- *(enabled by default)*— Causes all algorithms to compute and output a content size for each node
- `detailed_layout_info`- *(enabled by default)*— Causes algorithms to stores detailed information of the nodes in TaffyTree, with only CSS Grid supporting this.
- `strict_provenance`

[§](https://docs.rs#taffy-tree)Taffy Tree

- `taffy_tree`- *(enabled by default)*— Enable the built-in Taffy node tree. See- `TaffyTree`

[§](https://docs.rs#other)Other

- `serde`- `serde`
- `parse`- `FromStr`trait for Taffy style types
- `parse_faster`- `parse`feature with proc-macro dependent optimisations
- `std`- *(enabled by default)*— Allow Taffy to depend on the- `Rust Standard Library`
- `alloc`- *(enabled by default)*— Allow Taffy to depend on the alloc library
- `debug`
- `profile`

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [compute](https://docs.rs/compute/index.html)
- Low-level access to the layout algorithms themselves. For a higher-level API, see the `TaffyTree`
- [geometry](https://docs.rs/geometry/index.html)
- Geometric primitives useful for layout
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Commonly used types
- [style](https://docs.rs/style/index.html)
- A typed representation of [CSS style properties](https://css-tricks.com/snippets/css/a-guide-to-flexbox/)in Rust. Used as input to layout computation.
- [style_](https://docs.rs/style_helpers/index.html)- helpers
- Helper functions which it make it easier to create instances of types in the `style`and`geometry`modules.
- [tree](https://docs.rs/tree/index.html)
- Contains both a high-level interface to Taffy using a ready-made node tree, and a set of traits for defining custom node trees.
- [util](https://docs.rs/util/index.html)
- Helpful misc. utilities such as a function to debug print a tree

- Error type for parsing a type from string

- A typed representation of the CSS style information for a single node.
- [Taffy](https://docs.rs/struct.TaffyTree.html)- Tree - `taffy_tree`
- An entire tree of UI nodes. The entry point to Taffy’s high-level API.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Cache](https://docs.rs/trait.CacheTree.html)- Tree
- Trait used by the `compute_cached_layout`method which allows cached layout results to be stored and retrieved.
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/trait.LayoutBlockContainer.html)- Block - Container - `block_layout`

- [Layout](https://docs.rs/trait.LayoutFlexboxContainer.html)- Flexbox - Container - `flexbox`
- Extends `LayoutPartialTree`
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/trait.LayoutGridContainer.html)- Grid - Container - `grid`
- Extends `LayoutPartialTree`
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/trait.LayoutPartialTree.html)- Partial - Tree
- Any type that implements `LayoutPartialTree`[Taffy’s algorithms](https://docs.rs/compute/index.html)
- [Print](https://docs.rs/trait.PrintTree.html)- Tree
- Trait used by the `print_tree`method which prints a debug representation
- [Round](https://docs.rs/trait.RoundTree.html)- Tree
- Trait used by the `round_layout`method which takes a tree of unrounded float-valued layouts and performs rounding to snap the values to the pixel grid.
- [Traverse](https://docs.rs/trait.TraversePartialTree.html)- Partial - Tree
- Taffy’s abstraction for downward tree traversal.
- [Traverse](https://docs.rs/trait.TraverseTree.html)- Tree
- A marker trait which extends `TraversePartialTree`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_block_layout.html)- block_ - layout - `block_layout`
- Computes the layout of `LayoutPartialTree`
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_cached_layout.html)- cached_ - layout
- Attempts to find a cached layout for the specified node and layout inputs.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_flexbox_layout.html)- flexbox_ - layout - `flexbox`
- Computes the layout of a box according to the flexbox algorithm
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_grid_layout.html)- grid_ - layout - `grid`
- Grid layout algorithm This consists of a few phases:
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_hidden_layout.html)- hidden_ - layout
- Creates a layout for this node and its children, recursively. Each hidden node has zero size and is placed at the origin
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_leaf_layout.html)- leaf_ - layout
- Compute the size of a leaf node (node with no children)
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_root_layout.html)- root_ - layout
- Compute layout for the root node in the tree
- [print_](https://docs.rs/fn.print_tree.html)- tree - `std`
- Prints a debug representation of the computed layout for a tree of nodes, starting with the passed root node.
- [round_](https://docs.rs/fn.round_layout.html)- layout
- Rounds the calculated layout to exact pixel values

# unicode_segmentation - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicode-segmentation/^1.13/

## Expand description

Iterators which split strings on Grapheme Cluster, Word, or Sentence boundaries, according
to the [Unicode Standard Annex #29](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/) rules.

```
use unicode_segmentation::UnicodeSegmentation;
fn main() {
    let s = "a̐éö̲\r\n";
    let g = s.graphemes(true).collect::<Vec<&str>>();
    let b: &[_] = &["a̐", "é", "ö̲", "\r\n"];
    assert_eq!(g, b);
    let s = "The quick (\"brown\") fox can't jump 32.3 feet, right?";
    let w = s.unicode_words().collect::<Vec<&str>>();
    let b: &[_] = &["The", "quick", "brown", "fox", "can't", "jump", "32.3", "feet", "right"];
    assert_eq!(w, b);
    let s = "The quick (\"brown\")  fox";
    let w = s.split_word_bounds().collect::<Vec<&str>>();
    let b: &[_] = &["The", " ", "quick", " ", "(", "\"", "brown", "\"", ")", "  ", "fox"];
    assert_eq!(w, b);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#no_std)no_std

unicode-segmentation does not depend on libstd, so it can be used in crates
with the `#![no_std]` attribute.

[§](https://docs.rs#cratesio)crates.io

You can use this package in your project by adding the following
to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
unicode-segmentation = "1"
```

# web_time - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/web-time/^1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#description)Description

Complete drop-in replacement for [ std::time](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/time/) that works in browsers.

Currently [ Instant::now()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.Instant.html#method.now) and

[will simply panic when using the](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html#method.now)

`SystemTime::now()``wasm32-unknown-unknown` target. This implementation uses
[for](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance/now)

`Performance.now()`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.Instant.html)

`Instant`[for](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date/now)

`Date.now()`[to offer a drop-in replacement that works in browsers.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html)

`SystemTime`At the same time the library will simply re-export [ std::time](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/time/) when not
using the

`wasm32-unknown-unknown` target and will not pull in any
dependencies.Additionally, if compiled with `target-feature = "atomics"` it will
synchronize the timestamps to account for different context’s, like web
workers. See [ Performance.timeOrigin](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance/timeOrigin) for more information.

Using `-Ctarget-feature=+nontrapping-fptoint` will improve the performance
of [ Instant::now()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.Instant.html#method.now) and

[, but the vast majority of the time is still spent going through JS.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html#method.now)

`SystemTime::now()`[§](https://docs.rs#target)Target

This library specifically targets browsers, that support
[ Performance.now()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance/now), with the

`wasm32-unknown-unknown` target. Emscripten
is not supported. WASI doesn’t require support as it has it’s own native API
to deal with [.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/time/)

`std::time`Furthermore it depends on [ wasm-bindgen](https://crates.io/crates/wasm-bindgen), which is required. This library
will continue to depend on it until a viable alternative presents itself, in
which case multiple ecosystems could be supported.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

[§](https://docs.rs#ticking-during-sleep)Ticking during sleep

Currently a known bug is affecting browsers on operating system other then
Windows. This bug prevents [ Instant](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.Instant.html) from continuing to tick when the
context is asleep. This doesn’t necessarily conflict with Rusts requirements
of

[, but might still be unexpected.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.Instant.html)

`Instant`See [the MDN documentation on this](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance/now#ticking_during_sleep) for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#context-support)Context support

The implementation of [ Instant::now()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.Instant.html#method.now) relies on the availability of the

[, a lack thereof will cause a panic. This can happen if called from a](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/performance_property)

`Performance` object[worklet](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Worklet).

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

You can simply import the types you need:

```
use web_time::{Instant, SystemTime};
let now = Instant::now();
let time = SystemTime::now();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)`serde`

Implements [ serde::Deserialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-unknown-unknown/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html) and

[for](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/wasm32-unknown-unknown/serde_core/ser/trait.Serialize.html)

`serde::Serialize`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html)

`SystemTime`[§](https://docs.rs#msrv)MSRV

As this library heavily relies on [ wasm-bindgen](https://crates.io/crates/wasm-bindgen) the MSRV depends on it.
At the point of time this was written the MSRV is 1.60.

[§](https://docs.rs#alternatives)Alternatives

[instant](https://crates.io/crates/instant) [ is a popular alternative! However the API it implements doesn’t match ](https://crates.io/crates/instant)[ std::time](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/time/) exactly.

# repose_ui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/repose-ui/0.21.1/target-redirect/repose_ui/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#views-modifiers-and-layout)Views, Modifiers, and Layout

Repose UI is built around three core ideas:

- `View`: an immutable description of a UI node.
- `Modifier`: layout, styling, and interaction hints attached to a- `View`.
- Layout + paint: a separate pass (`layout_and_paint`) that turns the`View`tree into a`Scene`+ hit regions using the Taffy layout engine.

[§](https://docs.rs#views)Views

A `View` is a lightweight value that describes *what* to show, not *how* it is
rendered. It is cheap to create and you are expected to rebuild the entire
view tree on each frame:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use repose_core::*;
use repose_ui::*;
fn Counter(count: i32, on_inc: impl Fn() + 'static) -> View {
    Column(Modifier::new().padding(16.0)).child((
        Text(format!("Count = {count}")),
        Button("Increment".into_children(), on_inc),
    ))
}
```
Internally, a `View` has:

- `id: ViewId`- assigned during composition/layout.
- `kind: ViewKind`- which widget it is (Text, Button, ScrollV, etc.).
- `modifier: Modifier`- layout/styling/interaction metadata.
- `children: Vec<View>`- owned child views.

Views are *pure data*: they do not hold state or references into platform
APIs. State lives in signals / `remember_*` and platform integration happens
in the runner (`repose-platform`).

[§](https://docs.rs#modifiers)Modifiers

`Modifier` describes *how* a view participates in layout and hit‑testing:

- Size hints: `size`,`width`,`height`,`min_size`,`max_size`,`fill_max_size`,`fill_max_width`,`fill_max_height`.
- Box model: `padding`,`padding_values`.
- Visuals: `background`,`background_brush`,`border`,`clip_rounded`,`alpha`,`transform`.
- Flex / grid: `flex_grow`,`flex_shrink`,`flex_basis`,`align_self`,`justify_content`,`align_items`,`grid`,`grid_span`.
- Positioning: `absolute()`,`offset(..)`for overlay / Stack / FABs.
- Interaction: `clickable()`, pointer callbacks,`on_scroll`,`semantics`.
- Custom paint: `painter`(used by`repose-canvas`).

Example:

```
use repose_core::*;
use repose_ui::*;
fn CardExample() -> View {
    Box(
        Modifier::new()
            .padding(16.0)
            .background(theme().surface)
            .border(1.0, theme().outline, 8.0)
            .clip_rounded(8.0),
    )
    .child(Text("Hello, Repose!"))
}
```
Modifiers are merged into a Taffy `Style` inside `layout_and_paint`. Most
values are specified in density‑independent pixels (dp) and converted to
physical pixels (`px`) using the current `Density` local.

[§](https://docs.rs#layout-1)Layout

Layout is a pure function:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
pub fn layout_and_paint(
    root: &View,
    size_px: (u32, u32),
    textfield_states: &HashMap<u64, Rc<RefCell<TextFieldState>>>,
    interactions: &Interactions,
    focused: Option<u64>,
) -> (Scene, Vec<HitRegion>, Vec<SemNode>);
```
It:

- Clones the root `View`and assigns stable`ViewId`s.
- Builds a parallel Taffy tree and computes layout for the given window size.
- Walks the tree to:
- Emit `SceneNode`s for visuals (rects, text, images, scrollbars, etc.).
- Build `HitRegion`s for input routing (clicks, pointer events, scroll).
- Build `SemNode`s for accessibility / semantics.

- Emit

`Row`, `Column`, `Stack`, `Grid`, `ScrollV` and `ScrollXY` are all special
`ViewKind`s that map into Taffy styles and additional paint/hit logic.

Because layout + paint are separate from the platform runner, you can reuse the same UI code on desktop, Android, and other platforms.

# repose_ui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/repose-ui/0.21.1/repose_ui/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#views-modifiers-and-layout)Views, Modifiers, and Layout

Repose UI is built around three core ideas:

- `View`: an immutable description of a UI node.
- `Modifier`: layout, styling, and interaction hints attached to a- `View`.
- Layout + paint: a separate pass (`layout_and_paint`) that turns the`View`tree into a`Scene`+ hit regions using the Taffy layout engine.

[§](https://docs.rs#views)Views

A `View` is a lightweight value that describes *what* to show, not *how* it is
rendered. It is cheap to create and you are expected to rebuild the entire
view tree on each frame:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use repose_core::*;
use repose_ui::*;
fn Counter(count: i32, on_inc: impl Fn() + 'static) -> View {
    Column(Modifier::new().padding(16.0)).child((
        Text(format!("Count = {count}")),
        Button("Increment".into_children(), on_inc),
    ))
}
```
Internally, a `View` has:

- `id: ViewId`- assigned during composition/layout.
- `kind: ViewKind`- which widget it is (Text, Button, ScrollV, etc.).
- `modifier: Modifier`- layout/styling/interaction metadata.
- `children: Vec<View>`- owned child views.

Views are *pure data*: they do not hold state or references into platform
APIs. State lives in signals / `remember_*` and platform integration happens
in the runner (`repose-platform`).

[§](https://docs.rs#modifiers)Modifiers

`Modifier` describes *how* a view participates in layout and hit‑testing:

- Size hints: `size`,`width`,`height`,`min_size`,`max_size`,`fill_max_size`,`fill_max_width`,`fill_max_height`.
- Box model: `padding`,`padding_values`.
- Visuals: `background`,`background_brush`,`border`,`clip_rounded`,`alpha`,`transform`.
- Flex / grid: `flex_grow`,`flex_shrink`,`flex_basis`,`align_self`,`justify_content`,`align_items`,`grid`,`grid_span`.
- Positioning: `absolute()`,`offset(..)`for overlay / Stack / FABs.
- Interaction: `clickable()`, pointer callbacks,`on_scroll`,`semantics`.
- Custom paint: `painter`(used by`repose-canvas`).

Example:

```
use repose_core::*;
use repose_ui::*;
fn CardExample() -> View {
    Box(
        Modifier::new()
            .padding(16.0)
            .background(theme().surface)
            .border(1.0, theme().outline, 8.0)
            .clip_rounded(8.0),
    )
    .child(Text("Hello, Repose!"))
}
```
Modifiers are merged into a Taffy `Style` inside `layout_and_paint`. Most
values are specified in density‑independent pixels (dp) and converted to
physical pixels (`px`) using the current `Density` local.

[§](https://docs.rs#layout-1)Layout

Layout is a pure function:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
pub fn layout_and_paint(
    root: &View,
    size_px: (u32, u32),
    textfield_states: &HashMap<u64, Rc<RefCell<TextFieldState>>>,
    interactions: &Interactions,
    focused: Option<u64>,
) -> (Scene, Vec<HitRegion>, Vec<SemNode>);
```
It:

- Clones the root `View`and assigns stable`ViewId`s.
- Builds a parallel Taffy tree and computes layout for the given window size.
- Walks the tree to:
- Emit `SceneNode`s for visuals (rects, text, images, scrollbars, etc.).
- Build `HitRegion`s for input routing (clicks, pointer events, scroll).
- Build `SemNode`s for accessibility / semantics.

- Emit

`Row`, `Column`, `Stack`, `Grid`, `ScrollV` and `ScrollXY` are all special
`ViewKind`s that map into Taffy styles and additional paint/hit logic.

Because layout + paint are separate from the platform runner, you can reuse the same UI code on desktop, Android, and other platforms.

[318](#318)static DRAGVALUE_COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
[319](#319)
[320](#320)pub fn DragValue(
[325](#325)    value: f32,
[326](#326)    range: (f32, f32),
[327](#327)    speed: f32,
[328](#328)    on_change: impl Fn(f32) + 'static,
[329](#329)) -> View {
[330](#330)    let id = DRAGVALUE_COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
[331](#331)    let drag_start_x = remember_state_with_key(format!("dv_dsx_{}", id), || 0.0f32);
[332](#332)    let drag_start_val = remember_state_with_key(format!("dv_dsv_{}", id), || 0.0f32);
[333](#333)    let is_dragging = remember_state_with_key(format!("dv_drg_{}", id), || false);
[334](#334)
[335](#335)    let oc = Rc::new(on_change);
[336](#336)    let min = range.0;
[337](#337)    let max = range.1;
[338](#338)    let cur = value;
[339](#339)
[340](#340)    let th = locals::theme();
[341](#341)
[342](#342)    Box(Modifier::new()
[343](#343)        .min_width(48.0)
[344](#344)        .height(28.0)
[345](#345)        .background(th.surface_container)
[346](#346)        .border(1.0, th.outline, 4.0)
[347](#347)        .clip_rounded(4.0)
[348](#348)        .padding_values(PaddingValues {
[349](#349)            left: 4.0,
[350](#350)            right: 4.0,
[351](#351)            top: 0.0,
[352](#352)            bottom: 0.0,
[353](#353)        })
[354](#354)        .on_pointer_down({
[355](#355)            let dsx = drag_start_x.clone();
[356](#356)            let dsv = drag_start_val.clone();
[357](#357)            let drg = is_dragging.clone();
[358](#358)            move |pe: PointerEvent| {
[359](#359)                *drg.borrow_mut() = true;
[360](#360)                *dsx.borrow_mut() = pe.position.x;
[361](#361)                *dsv.borrow_mut() = cur;
[362](#362)            }
[363](#363)        })
[364](#364)        .on_pointer_move({
[365](#365)            let dsx = drag_start_x.clone();
[366](#366)            let dsv = drag_start_val.clone();
[367](#367)            let drg = is_dragging.clone();
[368](#368)            let oc = oc.clone();
[369](#369)            move |pe: PointerEvent| {
[370](#370)                if !*drg.borrow() {
[371](#371)                    return;
[372](#372)                }
[373](#373)                let dx = pe.position.x - *dsx.borrow();
[374](#374)                let new_val = (*dsv.borrow() + dx * speed).clamp(min, max);
[375](#375)                (oc)(new_val);
[376](#376)            }
[377](#377)        })
[378](#378)        .on_pointer_up({
[379](#379)            let drg = is_dragging.clone();
[380](#380)            move |_pe: PointerEvent| {
[381](#381)                *drg.borrow_mut() = false;
[382](#382)            }
[383](#383)        })
[384](#384)        .cursor(CursorIcon::EwResize))
[385](#385)    .child(
[386](#386)        Text(format_value(value))
[387](#387)            .size(13.0)
[388](#388)            .color(th.on_surface)
[389](#389)            .single_line()
[390](#390)            .overflow_ellipsize(),
[391](#391)    )
[392](#392)}

[394](#394)fn format_value(v: f32) -> String {
[395](#395)    if (v - v.round()).abs() < 1e-6 {
[396](#396)        format!("{}", v.round() as i64)
[397](#397)    } else if (v * 10.0 - (v * 10.0).round()).abs() < 1e-6 {
[398](#398)        format!("{:.1}", v)
[399](#399)    } else {
[400](#400)        format!("{:.2}", v)
[401](#401)    }

pub enum IntrinsicSizeMode {
    MinContent,
    MaxContent,
}
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MinContent)

### MinContent

Smallest size at which the view’s content does not overflow.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MaxContent)

### MaxContent

Largest size the view’s content would take if unconstrained.

# LazyColumn in repose_ui::lazy - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/repose-ui/0.21.1/repose_ui/lazy/fn.LazyColumn.html

```
pub fn LazyColumn<T, F, K, H>(
    items:
```
[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<T>,
    item_height: H,
    get_key: K,
    item_builder: F,
    config: [LazyColumnConfig](https://docs.rs/lazy_states/struct.LazyColumnConfig.html),
) -> [View](https://docs.rs/repose-core/0.21.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/repose_core/view/struct.View.html)## Expand description

Virtualized list - only renders visible items.

`item_height` may be a uniform `f32` (dp) or a per-item closure. For
heterogeneous heights, pass `|item| item.height_dp` to compute each
item’s height from its data.

Optionally animates item enter/exit when items are added or removed.
Provide `get_key` for stable item identity and `animate_spec` to enable
fade-in for new items and fade-out for removed items.

When `animate_spec` is `None`, behavior is identical to the original
(no item animations).

---

# LazyHorizontalGrid in repose_ui::lazy - Rust

pub fn LazyHorizontalGrid<T, F>(

Virtualized horizontally-scrolling grid with a fixed number of rows.

Items are arranged top-to-bottom, left-to-right. Only items visible in the
viewport (plus a buffer) are rendered. Each item has the same width (`item_width_dp`).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let state = Rc::new(LazyGridState::new());
LazyHorizontalGrid(
    3,                          // rows
    items,                      // Vec<MyItem>
    100.0,                      // item width in dp
    state,
    Modifier::new().fill_max_size().gap(8.0),
    |item, index| Card(Modifier::new().fill_max_height(), Text(format!("Item {index}"))),
)
```

# LazyVerticalGrid in repose_ui::lazy - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/repose-ui/0.21.1/repose_ui/lazy/fn.LazyVerticalGrid.html

```
pub fn LazyVerticalGrid<T, F>(
    columns:
```
[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    items: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<T>,

    item_builder: F,
    config: [LazyGridConfig](https://docs.rs/lazy_states/struct.LazyGridConfig.html),
) -> [View](https://docs.rs/repose-core/0.21.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/repose_core/view/struct.View.html)## Expand description

Virtualized scrolling grid with a fixed number of columns.

Items are arranged left-to-right, top-to-bottom. Only items visible in the
viewport (plus a buffer) are rendered. Each item has the same height (`item_height_dp`).

Supply row/column gaps via modifier methods on the `modifier` parameter:
`.row_gap(v)`, `.column_gap(v)`, or `.gap(v)` to set both.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let state = LazyGridState::new();
let state_rc = Rc::new(state);
LazyVerticalGrid(
    3,                          // columns
    items,                      // Vec<MyItem>
    120.0,                      // item height in dp
    state_rc.clone(),
    Modifier::new().fill_max_size().gap(8.0),
    |item, index| Card(Modifier::new().fill_max_width(), Text(format!("Item {index}"))),
)
```

# LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid in repose_ui::lazy - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/repose-ui/0.21.1/repose_ui/lazy/fn.LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid.html

```
pub fn LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid<T, F, K>(
    columns:
```
[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    items: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<T>,
    item_height_dp: K,
    item_builder: F,
    config: [LazyVerticalStaggeredGridConfig](https://docs.rs/lazy_states/struct.LazyVerticalStaggeredGridConfig.html),
) -> [View](https://docs.rs/repose-core/0.21.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/repose_core/view/struct.View.html)## Expand description

Virtualized staggered grid (Pinterest-style).

Items are arranged in a fixed number of columns. Each item can have a different height. Items are placed in the column with the least accumulated height, creating a staggered visual effect.

Only items visible in the viewport (plus a buffer) are rendered.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let state = Rc::new(LazyVerticalStaggeredGridState::new());
LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid(
    2,                          // columns
    items,                      // Vec<MyItem>
    |item: &MyItem| item.height_dp,  // per-item height
    state,
    Modifier::new().fill_max_size().gap(8.0),
    |item: &MyItem, index: usize| { /* ... */ },
)
```
